BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p273/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p273/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p273/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes God’s creation without a model from human making by a model; the author instead sees the form aḥsan as not straightforwardly derived from khalaqa / khāliq, but from the sense of khaliq (worthy).
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p273/r2.anchor: و"الراغب" في المفردات يفرق بين الخلق من الله على غير مثال، ومن الناس على مثال

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.claim: They describe human creation in stages from dust and reproductive fluid through clot, morsel, bone, and flesh, paralleling al-Mu’minun.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.anchor: ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظم ثم لحم

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.claim: It recounts human development from clay through a blood clot to another creation, recalling 22:5.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.anchor: reminiscent of 22:5, recounts a human being’s development starting from a clot of blood and culminating in another creation (vv. 12–14)

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.claim: The creation sequence in al-Mu’minūn describes the same reality as this passage and summarizes the stages that testify to resurrection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.anchor: The following verses of Sūrah al-Mu’minūn point to precisely the same reality:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r2.claim: The majority read both occurrences of bones in the plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور عظاما والعظام الجمع فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وأبان والمفضل والحسن وقتادة وهارون والجعفي ويونس عن أبي عمرو وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r3.claim: These readers use the singular for both occurrences of bones; singular here can denote the generic class.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وأبان والمفضل والحسن وقتادة وهارون والجعفي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r4.speaker: السلمي وقتادة والأعرج والأعمش ومجاهد وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r4.claim: These readers use singular for the first mention of bones and plural for the second; singular denotes the generic class.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r4.anchor: وقرأ السلمي وقتادة أيضا والأعرج والأعمش ومجاهد وابن محيصن بإفراد الأول وجمع الثاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء وإبراهيم بن أبي بكر ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r5.claim: These readers use plural for the first mention and singular for the second; singular denotes the generic class.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء وإبراهيم بن أبي بكر ومجاهد أيضا بجمع الأول وإفراد الثاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the singular replaces the plural without ambiguity because a person has many bones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وضع الواحد موضع الجمع لزوال اللبس لأن الإنسان ذو عظام كثيرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r7.speaker: سيبويه وأصحابنا
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r7.claim: Sībawayh and the author's grammatical school allow this singular-for-plural usage only in poetic necessity, citing a line about eating within part of one's belly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r7.anchor: وهذا لا يجوز عند سيبويه وأصحابنا إلا في الضرورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية والضحاك وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Shaʿbī, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Zayd say the final creation is the breathing of the spirit into the embryo.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية والضحاك وابن زيد، هو نفخ الروح فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also interprets the final creation as emergence into the world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r9.anchor: ابن عباس أيضا: خروجه إلى الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r10.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r10.claim: Another group interprets the final creation as the growth of the embryo's hair.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r11.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r11.claim: Mujāhid interprets the final creation as full maturity and youth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says the final creation is the person's ability to manage worldly affairs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا تصرفه في أمور الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah rejects narrowing the phrase to one feature: it covers speech and understanding, beginning with ensoulment and ending with acquired knowledge before death, as in a report from Ibn ʿAbbās.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r13.anchor: وهذا التخصيص لا وجه له وإنما هو عام في هذا وغيره من وجود النطق والإدراك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes the new creation as a distinct rational, speaking, hearing, seeing being whose members and parts contain wonders beyond description.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري ما ملخصه: خلقا آخر مباينا للخلق الأول مباينة ما أبعدها حيث جعله حيوانا ناطقا سميعا بصيرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r15.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r15.claim: Abū Ḥanīfah infers from calling the embryo a new creation that someone who steals an egg that hatches in his possession owes the egg, not the chick.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r15.anchor: وقد احتج أبو حنيفة بقوله خلقا آخر على أن غاصب بيضة أفرخت عنده يضمن البيضة ولا يرد الفرخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains إنشاء as bringing the spirit into the embryo and completing its creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r16.anchor: وقال أنشأناه جعل إنشاء الروح فيه وإتمام خلقه إنشاء له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r17.claim: The author says the passage refutes al-Naẓẓām's claim that the person is only a spirit and philosophers' claim that the person is indivisible, since God describes a composite being.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r17.anchor: وفي هذا رد على النظام في زعمه أن الإنسان هو الروح فقط، وقد بين تعالى أنه مركب من هذه الأشياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r18.claim: Tabāraka is a past verb that does not inflect; it means God is exalted and holy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r18.anchor: وتبارك فعل ماض لا يتصرف. ومعناه تعالى وتقدس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r1.claim: The parsing of أحسن as a superlative depends on whether its genitive addition to a definite noun is considered complete or incomplete: it is respectively an adjective or apposition; another view makes it predicate of an omitted هو.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r1.anchor: والخلاف فيها إذا أضيفت إلى معرفة هل إضافتها محضة أم غير محضة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r2.claim: Here creators means estimators; the word can also describe human makers, but is denied to humans only in the sense of originating creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r2.anchor: ومعنى الخالقين المقدرين وهو وصف يطلق على غير الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r3.speaker: الأعلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r3.claim: Al-Aʿlam explains Zuhayr's poem's creator as a leatherworker who measures, prepares, cuts, and sews leather; the image praises one who carries a prepared undertaking through without failure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r3.anchor: والخالق الذي لا يقدر الأديم ويهيئه لأن يقطعه ويخرزه والفري القطع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah glosses creator as maker and says the word applies to human craft, while its sense of origination is exclusive to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r4.anchor: معناه الصانعين يقال لمن صنع شيئا خلقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the plural creators is used because God granted Jesus permission to create.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: قال الخالقين لأنه أذن لعيسى في أن يخلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r6.claim: The compared dimension of أحسن is omitted because الخالقين supplies it: God is best in creating or estimating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r6.anchor: وتمييز أفعل التفضيل محذوف لدلالة الخالقين عليه، أي أحسن الخالقين خلقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r7.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r7.claim: A report says that when ʿUmar heard the account of human creation, he exclaimed that God is blessed, the best of creators, and the verse was then revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r7.anchor: وروي أن عمر لما سمع ولقد خلقنا الإنسان إلى آخره قال فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r8.speaker: معاذ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r8.claim: Another report names Muʿādh as the speaker of the phrase that preceded revelation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي سرح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r9.claim: A report says ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ said it; it became the cause of his apostasy, after which he returned to Islam and practiced well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p552/r9.anchor: عبد الله بن أبي سرح، وكانت سبب ارتداده ثم أسلم وحسن إسلامه

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r6.claim: God transforms the white semen into a red clot.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r6.anchor: بأن أحلنا النطفة البيضاء علقة حمراء

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib says ʿalaq is clotted blood, including the clot from which the child develops.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r7.anchor: قال الراغب : العلق الدم الجامد ومنه العلقة التي يكون منها الولد

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r8.claim: A muḍgha is a morsel of flesh that could be chewed, without distinct parts or features.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r8.anchor: المضغة لحم تمضع أي فصيرناها قطعة لحم لا استبانة ولا تمايز فيها

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r9.claim: The greater part of the morsel becomes bones, hardened after forty-three days and arranged as the body’s central support in wise forms and positions.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r9.anchor: بأن صلبناها بعد ثلاث وأربعين وجعلناها عمودا للبدن على هيئات وأوضاع

BURSEVI:v6p51/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51/r1.claim: The remaining flesh covers each bone in a fitting amount and arrangement; the Persian gloss describes flesh growing over veins, limbs, tendons, and muscles.
BURSEVI:v6p51/r1.anchor: كسونا كل عظم من تلك العظام ما يليق به من اللحم على مقدار لائق به وهيئات مناسبة له

BURSEVI:v6p51/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51/r2.claim: The differing conjunctions signal distinct transformations, and “bones” is plural because the bones vary.
BURSEVI:v6p51/r2.anchor: واختلاف العواطف للتنبيه على تفاوت الاستحالات وجمع العظام لاختلافها

BURSEVI:v6p51/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51/r3.claim: God brings him into another creation by breathing in the spirit; the Persian gloss continues through growth, weaning, maturity, and old age.
BURSEVI:v6p51/r3.anchor: {ثم أنشأناه} الإنشاء إيجاد الشيء وتربيته وأكثر ما يقال ذلك في الحيوان

BURSEVI:v6p51/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51/r4.claim: Thumma marks the great difference between the two creations.

BURSEVI:v6p51/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v6p51/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that someone who usurps an egg and it hatches in his possession owes compensation for the egg, not the chick, since it is another creation.
BURSEVI:v6p51/r5.anchor: واحتج به أبو حنيفة رحمه الله على أن من غصب بيضة فأفرخت عنده لزمه ضمان البيضة

BURSEVI:v6p51/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51/r6.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v6p51/r6.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima asks why God used stages if creating humans instantly would better show power and avoid suggesting causes.
BURSEVI:v6p51/r6.anchor: قال في "الأسئلة المقحمة" : خلق الله الآدمي أطوارا ولو خلقه دفعة واحدة

BURSEVI:v6p51/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51/r7.claim: The response is that staged transformation displays divine power more fully: homogeneous semen becomes diverse substances and organs, each with a wondrous structure and function.
BURSEVI:v6p51/r7.anchor: فالجواب لا بل الخلق بتقليب الأعيان واختراع الأشخاص أظهر في القدرة

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r1.claim: Bursevī glosses tabāraka as God’s exalted state, grounded in His comprehensive knowledge and overwhelming power.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r1.anchor: فتعالى شأنه من علمه الشامل وقدرته الباهرة

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r2.claim: Aḥsan al-khāliqīn is appositional to the divine name; khāliqīn means estimators, with the distinguishing noun omitted, and the excellence concerns the creation.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r2.anchor: بدل من الجلالة أي أحسن الخالقين خلقا أي المقدرين تقديرا حذف المميز لدلالة الخالقين عليه

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r3.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r3.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima objects that the verse makes humans creators of their acts, with God only the best creator.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r3.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : هذا يدل على أن العبد خالق أفعاله ويكون الرب أحسن منه

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r4.claim: The response is that khāliqīn means image-makers: no human image-maker can equal the Creator or breathe spirit into an image; Qurʾānic khalaqa can mean forming an image.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r4.anchor: فالجواب معناه أحسن المصورين لأن المصور يصور الصورة ويشكلها

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r5.claim: The Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the human as a new and supremely proportioned creation, with the greatest preparedness, honor, rank, and distinction.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة} يعني خلقا غير المخلوقات

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r6.claim: The human is the repository of gnosis, object of divine love and care; God praises Himself at this creation because the human is the best creature.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r6.anchor: لأنه خلق أحسن المخلوقين حيث جعله معدن العرفان وموضع المحبة ومتعلق العناية

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r7.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r7.claim: The Mathnawī verses celebrate the honor of “We ennobled” and “We favored” and urge reading al-Tīn on the human’s excellent form.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r7.anchor:
وفي "المثنوي" :
أي رخ زن زهرهاست شمس الضحى
أي كداي رنك توكلكونها
تاج كرمناست بر فرق سرت
طوق فضلناست آويزبرت

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r8.speaker: بعضي اهل وجدان
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r8.claim: Some people of spiritual insight say humans cannot adequately praise God after their stages of growth are described, so God praises Himself in this verse.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r8.anchor: بعضي ازاهل وجدان كويندكه ون درين آيت أحوال بني آدم وترقي ازمقامي بمقامي بيان فرموده

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي سرح
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r9.claim: A report says the revelation scribe ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ uttered “another creation” before the Prophet dictated it, then doubted and claimed he too received revelation; the source says he either converted at the conquest or died in disbelief.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r9.anchor: روي : أن عبد الله بن أبي سرح كان يكتب لرسول الله الوحي

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r10.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r10.claim: When the verse was revealed, ʿUmar independently said “Blessed is God, the best of creators”; the Prophet told him that it had been revealed in that form, and ʿUmar cherished the agreement.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r10.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية قال عمر رضي الله عنه فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين فقال عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r11.claim: These reports do not undermine Qurʾānic inimitability: a human’s coincident phrase is not comparable to the amount of a complete shortest sūra.
BURSEVI:v6p51#2/r11.anchor: لا يقال قد تكلم البشر ابتداء بمثل نظم القرآن وذلك فادح في إعجازه لما أن الخارج عن قدرة البشر

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r1.claim: The third stage changes semen from its former qualities into the qualities of an ʿalaqa, a clotted mass of blood.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r1.anchor: أي حولنا النطفة عن صفاتها إلى صفات العلقة وهي الدم الجامد

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r2.claim: A muḍgha is a piece of flesh about the size of a morsel one could chew, like a gharfa is a quantity one could scoop.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r2.anchor: أي جعلنا ذلك الدم الجامد مضغة أي قطعة لحم كأنها مقدار ما يمضغ كالغرفة وهي مقدار ما يغترف

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r3.claim: Calling this transformation “creation” means God removes some of the mass’s accidents, creates other accidents, and adds further parts.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r3.anchor: وسمى التحويل خلقا لأنه سبحانه يفني بعض أعراضها ويخلق أعراضا غيرها

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the word as singular ʿaẓm, intended collectively, as in the expression “rank upon rank.”
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر عظما والمراد منه الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r5.claim: The wording pictures flesh as clothing because it covers the bones.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r5.anchor: وذلك لأن اللحم يستر العظم فجعله كالكسوة لها

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r6.claim: The seventh stage is a radically distinct creation: formerly inert and mute, the human becomes living, articulate, hearing, and seeing, with wonders of wisdom in every part.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r6.anchor: أي خلقا مباينا للخلق الأول مباينة

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r7.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r7.claim: Al-ʿAwfī reports Ibn Abbas’s view that the phrase covers God’s development of a person after birth through childhood, youth, understanding, and intellect until death.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : هو تصريف الله إياه

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r8.claim: The postnatal-life interpretation is supported by the next verse’s statement that people will later die; Rāzī also says this meaning is reported from Ibn Abbas and Ibn ʿUmar.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r8.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي أيضا عن ابن عباس وابن عمر

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r9.claim: The verb “created anew” suits the creation of the spirit within the human and the completion of his formation.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r9.anchor: لأنه جعل إنشاء الروح فيه ، وإتمام خلقه إنشاء له

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r10.claim: Rāzī treats the description of the human as a composite of these created traits as evidence against al-Naẓẓām’s claim that the human is the spirit rather than the body.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r10.anchor: قالوا في الآية دلالة على بطلان قول النظام في أن الإنسان هو الروح لا البدن

RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r11.claim: He also says the verse refutes philosophers who describe the human as indivisible and not a body.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74#2/r11.anchor: وفيها دلالة أيضا على بطلان قول الفلاسفة

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r1.claim: Tabāraka can mean that God is exalted, since blessing involves extension or increase and what increases rises above what it exceeds.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r1.anchor: فإن البركة يرجع معناها إلى الامتداد والزيادة

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r2.claim: Alternatively, all blessings and good things come from God, who therefore deserves praise and reverence.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r2.anchor: والبركات والخيرات كلها من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r3.speaker: قول
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r3.claim: Another etymology derives the expression from burūk, stability: God is enduring and everlasting, and all blessings come from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r3.anchor: وقيل أصله من البروك وهو الثبات

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r4.claim: Aḥsan al-khāliqīn means “best of estimators”; the understood qualifier “in estimation” is omitted because the word “creators” indicates it.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r4.anchor: أي أحسن المقدرين تقديرا فترك ذكر المميز لدلالة الخالقين عليه

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that calling God the best creator presupposes other creators; humans create their acts by deliberate estimation, just as humans can be described as wise judges or merciful.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r5.anchor: قالت المعتزلة لولا أن الله تعالى قد يكون خالقا لفعله إذا قدره لما جاز القول بأنه أحسن الخالقين

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r6.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r6.claim: Al-Kaʿbī says a human may be called a creator only with a qualification, just as someone may be “master of a house” but not simply “Lord.”
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r6.anchor: قال الكعبي هذه الآية ، وإن دلت على أن العبد خالق

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r7.claim: Rāzī rejects explaining the plural as referring only to Jesus: the plural is broader, and if Jesus counts as a creator, image-makers would too.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r7.anchor: الذين هم جمع فحمله على عيسى خاصة لا يصح

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r8.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r8.claim: Rāzī’s fellow theologians answer that God is creator of everything (39:62), so “best creators” means best in people’s belief, as “easier for Him” is likewise contextual (30:27).
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r8.anchor: وأجاب أصحابنا بأن هذه الآية معارضة

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r9.claim: Another answer takes creator to mean estimator; but estimation as conjecture or calculation is impossible for God, making the verse among the ambiguous texts.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r9.anchor: هو أن الخالق هو المقدر لأن الخلق هو التقدير

RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r10.claim: Even if a human is a creator in the sense of estimating, that does not establish that a human originates things.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75/r10.anchor: لكن لم قلت بأنه خالق بمعنى كونه موجدا

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that if everything God creates is good and wise, He cannot create unbelief or sin; therefore humans must originate those acts.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r1.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الآية تدل على أن كل ما خلقه حسن وحكمة وصواب وإلا لما جاز وصفه بأنه أحسن الخالقين

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r2.claim: Rāzī answers that “good” can mean exact construction and composition; even if it means goodness and wisdom, all acts are good from God, who is bound by no higher command or prohibition.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r2.anchor: من الناس من حمل الحسن على الإحكام والاتقان في التركيب والتأليف

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, in al-Kalbī’s report, says ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ was dictating these verses; when he heard “a different creation,” he exclaimed “Blessed is God, best of creators,” and Muhammad told him to write it as revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r3.anchor: روى الكلبي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن عبدالله بن سعد بن أبي سرح كان يكتب هذه الآيات

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r4.claim: In the same report, ʿAbd Allāh doubted Muhammad’s claim, fled to Mecca, and is said either to have died an unbeliever or to have converted at the conquest; Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r4.anchor: فهرب إلى مكة فقيل إنه مات على الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports Ibn Abbas’s account that ʿUmar uttered the phrase when the verse was revealed and Muhammad told him it had been revealed that way.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r5.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال لما نزلت هذه الآية قال عمر بن الخطاب

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r6.claim: ʿUmar said God had agreed with him on four occasions: prayer behind the Station, the veil, his admonition to the Prophet’s wives (followed by 66:5), and this phrase.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r6.anchor: وكان عمر يقول : وافقني ربي في أربع

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r7.speaker: العارفون
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r7.claim: The gnostics say the episode brought ʿUmar good fortune and ʿAbd Allāh misery, illustrating that revelation guides some and misleads others (2:26).
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r7.anchor: قال العارفون هذه الواقعة كانت سبب السعادة لعمر

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r8.speaker: عبدالله بن سعد بن أبي سرح
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r8.claim: The account has ʿAbd Allāh object that a human had spoken words resembling the Qur’an, which seemed to undermine its inimitability.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r8.anchor: قد تكلم البشر ابتداء بمثل نظم القرآن ، وذلك يقدح في كونه معجزا كما ظنه عبدالله

RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r9.claim: Rāzī answers that this is possible if the utterance remained at a level where the Qur’an’s miraculous quality was not evident, removing ʿAbd Allāh’s objection.
RAZI-FULL:v23p75#2/r9.anchor: هذا غير مستبعد إذا كان قدره القدر الذي لا يظهر فيه الإعجاز فسقطت شبهة عبدالله

STUDYQURAN:23:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r1.claim: The clot and lump of flesh refer to the stages of physical human growth, discussed in the commentary on 22:5–6.
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r1.anchor: On the blood clot and lump of flesh, see 22:5–6c, which also discusses the stages of the physical growth of human beings.

STUDYQURAN:23:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r2.claim: One interpretation is that the spirit is breathed into what previously existed only as a form.
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r2.anchor: Brought him into being as another creation is interpreted variously as the inbreathing of the spirit into what was previously only a form (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:23:14/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the phrase to mean the act of being born.

STUDYQURAN:23:14/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r4.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r4.claim: A further interpretation is development into mature adulthood and full realization of one's faculties.
STUDYQURAN:23:14/r4.anchor: one’s development into mature adulthood and the full realization of one’s faculties (Q, R).

TAB-FULL:v17p20#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p20#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p20#2/r1.claim: God placed the human made from clay’s extract as a drop in the secure womb, prepared to hold it until its appointed development.

TAB-FULL:v17p21/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p21/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p21/r1.claim: God made the lump of flesh into bones. Most Hijazi and Iraqi readers recite bones in the plural; Asim and Abdullah read the two occurrences as singular ʿaẓm, but al-Tabari chooses the plural because the authoritative readers agree on it.

TAB-FULL:v17p22/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r1.claim: God clothed the bones with flesh; the pronoun in the following phrase may refer to the human named in 15:26 or to the bone, drop, and lump treated as one entity.
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r1.anchor: قوله: {ولقد خلقنا الإنسان} [الحجر: 26] قد يجوز أن تكون من ذكر العظم

TAB-FULL:v17p22/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r2.claim: Abdullah’s reading says God formed the drop into bone and sinew, then clothed it with flesh.
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r2.anchor: قد يجوز أن تكون من ذكر العظم والنطفة والمضغة، جعل ذلك كله كالشيء الواحد،

TAB-FULL:v17p22/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، الشعبي، مجاهد، أبو العالية، الضحاك، ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and the other named early authorities identify the new creation as the spirit being breathed into the body, making it human.
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r3.anchor: عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} [المؤمنون: 14] قال: نفخ الروح فيه "

TAB-FULL:v17p22/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that the new creation means the changing conditions after birth, including childhood, growth, nourishment, hair, and teeth.
TAB-FULL:v17p22/r4.anchor: تصريفه إياه في الأحوال بعد الولادة

TAB-FULL:v17p24/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the further creation as postnatal development: crying, finding the breast, moving, sitting, crawling, walking, weaning, eating, reaching puberty, and later maturity.
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين} [المؤمنون: 14] يقول: " خرج من بطن أمه بعد ما خلق،

TAB-FULL:v17p24/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r2.claim: Qatada transmits two explanations: growth of hair or the breathing of the spirit.
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} [المؤمنون: 14] قال: يقول بعضهم: هو نبات الشعر، وبعضهم يقول: هو نفخ الروح "

TAB-FULL:v17p24/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the new creation is after birth, with the child’s age and hair developing.
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r3.anchor: الضحاك: {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} [المؤمنون: 14] قال: «يقال الخلق الآخر بعد خروجه من بطن أمه بسنه وشعره»

TAB-FULL:v17p24/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r4.claim: Mujahid says the new creation occurs when youth reaches maturity.
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} [المؤمنون: 14] قال: «حين استوى شبابه»

TAB-FULL:v17p24/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers ensoulment: the spirit transforms the drop, clot, flesh, and bones into a human, as the spirit transformed Adam’s clay into a human being.
TAB-FULL:v17p24/r5.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: عنى بذلك نفخ الروح فيه؛ وذلك أنه بنفخ الروح فيه يتحول خلقا آخر إنسانا،

TAB-FULL:v17p25/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r1.claim: Mujahid says people make things, but God makes them best and is the best maker.
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين} [المؤمنون: 14] قال: «يصنعون ويصنع الله، والله خير الصانعين»

TAB-FULL:v17p25/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports the view that the wording responds to Jesus son of Mary creating, affirming that God creates better than Jesus did.
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج، في قوله: {فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين} [المؤمنون: 14] قال: عيسى ابن مريم يخلق

TAB-FULL:v17p25/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Mujahid’s explanation because Arabic calls every maker a khāliq; Zuhayr’s poetry uses the word for a craftsman who fashions something.
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r3.anchor: لأن العرب تسمي كل صانع خالقا؛ ومنه قول زهير: [البحر الكامل] ولأنت تفري ما خلقت

TAB-FULL:v17p25/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r4.claim: Zuhayr’s verse, also transmitted with a variant wording, contrasts someone who fashions and completes what he makes with people who make but fail to finish it.
TAB-FULL:v17p25/r4.anchor: ويروى: ولأنت تخلق ما فريت وبع … ض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.claim: After describing believers' virtues, the passage explains human creation and provision to show that God alone is Lord of humanity and all things and alone deserves worship.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.anchor: عقبه بشرح خلقهم وخلق ما أنعم عليهم من النعم مقرونا بتدبير أمرهم

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r8.claim: The author says he explained this verse's individual terms earlier in his discussion of 22:5.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r8.anchor: تقدم بيان مفردات الآية في الآية 5 من سورة الحج في الجزء السابق من الكتاب

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r9.claim: “We clothed the bones with flesh” is a subtle implied metaphor.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r9.anchor: وفي قوله { فكسونا العظام لحما } استعارة بالكناية لطيفة

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r10.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r10.claim: Al-Rāghib explains inshāʾ as bringing something into existence and nurturing it, as in the terms nashʾ and nashʾa.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r10.anchor: إيجاد الشيء وتربيته كما أن النشء والنشأة إحداثه

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r11.claim: Changing from khalq to inshāʾ marks a novel being not contained in prior matter: life, knowledge, and power have no counterpart in the drop, clot, morsel, or clothed bones, so the human self is newly brought into being.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r11.anchor: للدلالة على حدوث أمر حديث ما كان يتضمنه ولا يقارنه ما تقدمه من مادة

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r1.claim: The pronoun in “We brought him into being” refers to the human whose bones had been clothed with flesh; he is transformed from dead, ignorant, powerless matter into a living, knowing, capable being.

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r2.claim: The person is the former matter insofar as it becomes human, but is not identical with that matter: its essence and properties differ, with only a union in which the person uses the body as a tool, like a writer uses a pen.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r2.anchor: فهو تلك المادة السابقة فإنها التي صارت إنسانا

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r3.claim: The discussion links the distinction of person and body to 32:10–11: at death the human is taken, while the body is scattered in the earth.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الذي يستفاد من مثل قوله وقالوا أئذا ضللنا في الأرض إنا لفي خلق جديد

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.claim: One grammatical account uses thumma for stages separated by a complete break, while fa marks the closer succession of clot-to-morsel, morsel-to-bones, and bones-to-flesh.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.anchor: وقد قيل في وجهه أن ما عطف بثم له بينونة كاملة مع ما عطف عليه

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r5.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib traces tabāraka to baraka, permanence or settledness; baraka is enduring divine good within a thing, like water remaining in a pool.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r5.anchor: والبركة ثبوت الخير الإلهي في الشيء

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r6.claim: God's tabāraka means He uniquely possesses abundant good and freely pours it upon creation; this good is realized through His measuring and bringing things into existence.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r6.anchor: فالتبارك منه تعالى اختصاصه بالخير الكثير الذي يجود به ويفيضه على خلقه

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r7.claim: Because khalq originally means measuring and proportioning, God's arrangement of parts to fit one another and their surroundings generates abundant good.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r7.anchor: وهو إيجاد الأشياء وتركيب أجزائها بحيث تتناسب فيما بين أنفسها وتناسب ما وراءها

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r8.claim: “Best of creators” does not make creation exclusive to God: other beings also create in the sense of estimating or forming, a usage found elsewhere in the Qur'an.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r8.anchor: ووصفه تعالى بأحسن الخالقين يدل على عدم اختصاص الخلق به وهو كذلك لما تقدم

TABRISI:23:12-19/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:12-19/r1.claim: One explanation says God deserves exaltation because He is eternal, without beginning or end; baraka derives from firmness and stability.
TABRISI:23:12-19/r1.anchor: استحق التعظيم بأنه قديم لم يزل ولا يزال لأنه مأخوذ من البروك الذي هو الثبوت

TABRISI:23:12-19/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:12-19/r2.claim: God is the best creator because His creation has no defect; khalq originally means measuring, as when leather is measured before cutting.
TABRISI:23:12-19/r2.anchor: وقال أحسن الخالقين لأنه لا تفاوت في خلقه وأصل الخلق التقدير، يقال خلقت الأديم

TABRISI:23:12-19/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r3.speaker: حذيفة
TABRISI:23:12-19/r3.claim: Ḥudhayfa says, “You make things and God makes things, and He is the best of makers.”
TABRISI:23:12-19/r3.anchor: وقال حذيفة في هذه الآية تصنعون ويصنع الله وهو خير الصانعين

TABRISI:23:12-19/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:12-19/r4.claim: The wording shows that “creating” may be attributed to beings other than God, though creation in its true sense belongs only to God.
TABRISI:23:12-19/r4.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن اسم الخلق قد يطلق على فعل غير الله تعالى إلا أن الحقيقة في الخلق لله سبحانه فقط

TABRISI:23:12-19/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:12-19/r5.claim: True creation is bringing something into existence with exact measure and no disparity, as supported by the verse “His are creation and command.”
TABRISI:23:12-19/r5.anchor: فإن المراد من الخلق إيجاد الشيء مقدرا تقديرا لا تفاوت فيه وهذا إنما يكون من الله سبحانه وتعالى

TABRISI:23:12-19/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح
TABRISI:23:12-19/r6.claim: A report says that when the Prophet dictated “another creation,” Ibn Abī Sarḥ anticipated “Blessed is God, the best of creators,” then claimed prophethood and defected to Mecca.
TABRISI:23:12-19/r6.anchor: عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح كان يكتب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما بلغ إلى قوله

TABRISI:23:12-19/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:12-19/r7.claim: The author says that, if the report is sound, this coincidence is not miraculous or impossible; Ibn Abī Sarḥ was confused or self-deceived by disbelief and envy.
TABRISI:23:12-19/r7.anchor: ولو صح هذا فإن هذا القدر لا يكون معجزا ولا يمتنع أن يتفق ذلك من الواحد منا

TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.claim: The account contradicts al-Naẓẓām’s view that the human being is a spirit and Maʿmar’s view that a human is an indivisible, nonbodily thing.
TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على فساد قول النظام في أن الإنسان هو الروح وقول معمر إن الإنسان شيء لا ينقسم وإنه ليس بجسم

THALABI:v7p41#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p41#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p41#2/r4.claim: The verse describes the successive transformation of the drop into a clinging clot, a morsel, and then bones.
THALABI:v7p41#2/r4.anchor: ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة فخلقنا المضغة عظاما

THALABI:v7p41#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p41#2/r5.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم والآخرون
THALABI:v7p41#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr reporting from ʿĀṣim, read the two occurrences of bone in the singular, matching flesh in the singular; the others read the plural because a person has many bones.
THALABI:v7p41#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر عظما على الواحد في الحرفين، ومثله روى أبو بكر عن عاصم

THALABI:v7p41#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p41#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p41#2/r6.claim: The phrase means that God clothed the bones with flesh.
THALABI:v7p41#2/r6.anchor: فكسونا فألبسنا العظام لحما ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر

THALABI:v7p41#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p41#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والشعبي وعكرمة وأبو العالية والضحاك وابن زيد
THALABI:v7p41#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Shaʿbī, ʿIkrimah, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Zayd interpret the later creation as breathing the spirit into the fetus.
THALABI:v7p41#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والشعبي وعكرمة وأبو العالية والضحاك وابن زيد: نفخ الروح فيه.

THALABI:v7p42/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r1.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p42/r1.claim: Qatada explains the new creation as the growth of teeth and hair.
THALABI:v7p42/r1.anchor: قتادة: نبات الأسنان والشعر. ابن عمر: استواء الشباب

THALABI:v7p42/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v7p42/r2.claim: Ibn Umar interprets the new creation as reaching youthful maturity; this is also transmitted from Mujahid through Ibn Abi Najih and Ibn Jurayj.
THALABI:v7p42/r2.anchor: ابن عمر: استواء الشباب، وهي رواية ابن أبي نجيح وابن جريج عن مجاهد

THALABI:v7p42/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p42/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the phrase means the changing stages after birth: crying, finding the breast, sitting, crawling, standing, walking, weaning, eating, puberty, and traveling about.
THALABI:v7p42/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: إن ذلك تصريف أحواله بعد الولادة، يقول: خرج من بطن أمه

THALABI:v7p42/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r4.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p42/r4.claim: One reported interpretation of the new creation is the distinction of male and female.
THALABI:v7p42/r4.anchor: وقيل: الذكورة والأنوثية، وقيل: إعطاء العقل والفهم

THALABI:v7p42/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r5.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p42/r5.claim: Another reported interpretation of the new creation is the gift of reason and understanding.
THALABI:v7p42/r5.anchor: وقيل: الذكورة والأنوثية، وقيل: إعطاء العقل والفهم

THALABI:v7p42/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p42/r6.claim: Tabaraka means God deserves exaltation and praise, since He always has been and always will be; the word derives from firmness or abiding.
THALABI:v7p42/r6.anchor: فتبارك الله أي استحق التعظيم والثناء بأنه لم يزل ولا يزال وأصله من البروك وهو الثبوت

THALABI:v7p42/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p42/r7.claim: Here the best creators means the best formers and estimators.
THALABI:v7p42/r7.anchor: أحسن الخالقين أي المصورين والمقدرين، مجاهد: يصنعون ويصنع الله

THALABI:v7p42/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p42/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses creators as those who make things, while God makes them best of all.
THALABI:v7p42/r8.anchor: مجاهد: يصنعون ويصنع الله والله خير الصانعين

THALABI:v7p42/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
THALABI:v7p42/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the plural acknowledges that Jesus created, while God creates better than what Jesus created.
THALABI:v7p42/r9.anchor: ابن جريج: إنما جمع الخالقين لأن عيسى كان يخلق، فأخبر جل ثناؤه

THALABI:v7p42/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r10.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v7p42/r10.claim: Abu Qatada reports that when the verse through its end was revealed, Umar said, “Blessed is God, the best of creators,” and that phrase was then revealed.
THALABI:v7p42/r10.anchor: عن أبي قتادة قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية إلى آخرها قال عمر بن الخطاب

THALABI:v7p42/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p42/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p42/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the scribe Abd Allah ibn Abi Sarh anticipated the closing phrase, then claimed prophethood and defected to Mecca as an unbeliever.
THALABI:v7p42/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان ابن أبي سرح يكتب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأملى عليه هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r1.claim: The stages through the lump are explained earlier in the embryology passage in Sūrat al-Ḥajj.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r1.anchor: مفسر في سورة الحج إلى قوله: {فخلقنا المضغة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r2.claim: Both occurrences are also read in the singular, ʿaẓman.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r3.claim: Singular and plural are valid: a person has many bones, a singular can imply a collection, and nearby flesh and the generic noun support that sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3): التوحيد والجمع هاهنا جائزان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r4.claim: The plural better matches Qurʾānic usage elsewhere; the singular is possible as a generic noun denoting a class or collection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو علي: الجمع أشبه بما جاء في التنزيل في غير هذا الموضع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، مجاهد، الشعبي، عكرمة، الربيع، أبو العالية، ابن زيد، القتيبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and the listed authorities interpret the new creation as breathing the spirit into the embryo; al-Qutaybī selects this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني نفخ الروح فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r2.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r2.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the new creation is the growth of hair and teeth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو نبات الشعر والأسنان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r3.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, and Mujāhid in some transmissions, interpret it as reaching full youth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه قال: هو استواء الشباب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj offers another view: God made the embryo male or female.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r4.anchor: وحكى الزجاج قولا آخر وهو: أن جعل ذكرا وأنثى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r5.claim: The spirit interpretation is strongest: changed wording marks a new beginning when formerly lifeless flesh and bone become a living creature.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r6.claim: Once the embryo's bones and flesh are fully formed, it is a human child, and a slave woman carrying it becomes an umm walad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p540/r6.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن الجنين إذا استوى عظمه ولحمه على العظم فقد صار إنسانا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r1.claim: God deserves exaltation and praise, for He always has been and always will be.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r2.claim: Aḥsan al-khāliqīn means the best image-makers or measurers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r3.claim: In Arabic, khalq means measurement: leather is measured and fashioned to cut a flask, water skin, or shoe.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r4.claim: People make things, but God makes too, and God is the best maker.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: وتصنعون ويصنع الله، والله خير الصانعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r5.claim: A khāliq is a maker, and the feminine plural khāliqāt can refer to women makers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r5.anchor: قال الليث: رجل خالق، أي: صانع. وهن الخالقات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r6.claim: God's making is better than sculptors' images, which do not move; yakhluqūn here means they make.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p542/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان: يقول: هو أحسن خلقا من الذين يخلقون التماثيل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r9.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r9.claim: One reported interpretation of the “another creation” is the distinction of male and female.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r10.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r10.claim: Another reported interpretation of the “another creation” is the breathing of the spirit.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r11.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r11.claim: A further reported interpretation is the growth of hair and teeth.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r12.claim: God merits glorification and praise through the permanence of His existence.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r13.claim: God is the best of those who form and determine creation.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r4.claim: The embryo remains a drop for forty nights, then a clinging clot for forty nights, then a lump of flesh for forty nights.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r4.anchor: قوله: {ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة} [المؤمنون: 14] يكون في بطن أمه نطفة أربعين ليلة، ثم علقة أربعين ليلة، ثم يكون مضغة أربعين ليلة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r5.claim: One reading has the collective singular ʿaẓman, bones as a group; another has ʿiẓāman, bones one by one.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r5.anchor: قال: فخلقنا المضغة عظما يعني جماعة العظام في قراءة من قرأها: عظما. وهي تقرأ: عظاما يعني جماعة العظام عظما عظما.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r6.claim: Some also read the following word in the singular, al-ʿaẓm; the flesh phrase follows the same pattern as the preceding reading.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r6.anchor: {فكسونا العظام} [المؤمنون: 14] وبعضهم يقرأها العظم. {لحما} [المؤمنون: 14] وهي مثل الأولى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r7.claim: Qatāda explains the later creation as hair growing on the fetus.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r7.anchor: أبو سهل، عن أبي هلال الراسبي، عن قتادة قال: أنبت عليه الشعر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r8.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan is reported as identifying the later creation with the spirit.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r9.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r9.claim: In ʿAmr’s tafsīr, al-Ḥasan explains the later creation as male and female.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r9.anchor: وفي تفسير عمرو عن الحسن: ذكرا وأنثى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r10.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r10.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the later creation as the spirit while the child is still in the womb.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r10.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الروح وهو في بطن أمه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r11.speaker: أبو مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r11.claim: Ibn Mujāhid reports from his father that the later creation occurs when the person reaches full youth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r11.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: حين استوى به الشباب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r12.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r12.claim: “Blessed is God” invokes blessing, as “God is exalted” does at 23:116.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r12.anchor: قال: {فتبارك الله} [المؤمنون: 14] وهو من باب البركة كقوله: {فتعالى الله} [المؤمنون: 116]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r13.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r13.claim: People may make things resembling God’s creation, but they cannot breathe a spirit into them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r13.anchor: إن العباد قد يخلقون، يشبهون بخلق الله، ولا يستطيعون أن ينفخوا فيه الروح.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r14.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r14.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r14.claim: The Prophet says image-makers will be punished on the Resurrection Day and told to bring their creations to life.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r14.anchor: - الربيع بن صبيح، عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " المصورون يعذبون يوم القيامة ويقال لهم: أحيوا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r15.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r15.claim: Abū Hurayra reports God’s challenge to whoever imitates His creation: let them create a fly, speck, or mosquito.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r15.anchor: - أبو أمية بن يعلى الثقفي، عن سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " قال الله: من أظلم ممن يخلق كخلقي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r16.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r16.speaker: عائشة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r16.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet saying that those who imitate God’s creation will face the severest punishment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r16.anchor: - حماد، عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم، عن أبيه، عن عائشة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن أشد الناس عذابا يوم القيامة الذين يضاهون بخلق الله» .

QASHANI:23:14-22/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:14-22/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:14-22/r1.claim: The new creation comes by breathing God's spirit into the human and forming him in God's image: truly created, yet not merely a creature.
QASHANI:23:14-22/r1.anchor: { ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر } غير هذا المتقلب في أطوار الخلقة بنفخ روحنا فيه وتصويره بصورتنا

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r6.claim: God changes the nutfa into an alaqa by implantation or fertilization in the womb, making it a clinging, clot-like form.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r6.anchor: Sonra nutfeyi aleka halkettik rahime iliştirip telkīh yaptırarak tutturup pıhtı kan gibi bir tutuk hâline tahvil ettik.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r7.claim: Alaqa derives from attachment or clinging and can mean a sticky thing; al-Qāmūs also gives the meaning of clotted blood.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r7.anchor: “Aleka” esasen “ulûk” ve “ta‘alluk” gibi ilişmek ve yapışıp tutmak mânasından me’huz olarak ilişken, yapışkan şey demektir.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r8.speaker: Müfessirler
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r8.claim: Exegetes generally gloss alaqa as clotted blood, whereas the author identifies its primary referent as the attachment produced by fertilization in the womb.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r8.anchor: Müfessirler, umûmiyetle [3436] Dem-i câmid diye tefsir etmişler ise de asıl murad

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r9.claim: Mudgha is a morsel-sized piece of flesh, as if chewed.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r9.anchor: Alekayı mudga yarattık bir çiğnem et parçası hâline tahvil ettik.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r10.claim: The bones form the body's supporting framework and pillars.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r10.anchor: bunlar hikmetin muktezâsı üzere bedenin çatısını teşkil eden direkleridir.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r11.claim: Bones are created soft in the womb and harden after birth, like an egg's shell, which is soft in the hen and hardens outside.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r11.anchor: yumurtanın kabuğu tavuğun karnında iken yumuşak olup dışarı çıkınca sertleştiği gibi, kemikler de rahimde iken yumuşak ve çocuk doğduktan sonra tesallüb eder

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r12.claim: Each bone is furnished with fitting flesh, and the bones together are enveloped in a graceful covering of flesh.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r12.anchor: bütün o kemikler her birine münâsib birer et ile donatılarak hey’et-i mecmû‘ası zarif bir et kisvesiyle giydirilip kuşatıldı.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r13.claim: The final stage makes a wholly distinct human, with organs, spirit, faculties, and form, unlike any other creature; he connects this perfected form to al-Tīn 95:4.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r13.anchor: cehâzıyla, rûhuyla, kuvâsıyla, endâmıyla ona öyle güzel bir hilkat neş’eti verildi

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r14.claim: God is exalted as the source of every blessing and the creator of all; even if created principles or causes are called creators, God is the best creator.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r14.anchor: her şeyin hâlıkı O, O’nun halkından sonra vücûda gelen mebâdî ve esbâbın her biri bir hâlık addedilse ve bu suretle birçok hâlıklar farz olunsa, Allah bütün o hâlıkların en güzeli

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r15.claim: The first invention of every creation, refinement, development, and beauty belongs to God; all agency in other things ultimately belongs to Him.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r15.anchor: Her hilkatin, her ıstıfânın, her tekâmülün, her hüsnün ilk îcâdı, ilk numûnesi ancak O’nun ibdâ‘ı ve diğerlerindeki fâiliyetin bütün künhü O’nundur.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r16.claim: The quoted poem praises the hidden divine essence, the waves of God's creative art, the world as a witness to His existence, and His wisdom bringing beauty from dust.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r16.anchor: Bihâr-ı sun‘una emvâc peydâ ka‘r nâpeydâ Bülend ü pest-i âlem şâhid-i feyz-i vücûdundur

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r17.claim: Humans should not assume that their excellent creation makes them self-sufficient or absolves them of seeking felicity; they must strive to acquire the qualities described.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r17.anchor: İnsanlar böyle bambaşka bir neş’ette en güzel bir kıvam ile yaratılmış olduklarından dolayı kendilerini her murâda ermiş, felah ihtiyâcından müstağnî olmuş zannetmemelidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.claim: Although the creation verbs are past tense in Arabic, the author renders them in the present because the process of each person's creation continues.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.anchor: Bu bölümde geçen “yaratıyoruz, getiriyoruz” gibi fiillerin asılları âyetlerin metninde geçmiş zamanlıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.claim: Qur'anic past-tense forms can serve, among other purposes, to emphasize that the reported information is certain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.anchor: Kur’an’da verilen bilginin kesinliğine işaret etmek gibi bazı sebeplerle şimdiki, gelecek veya geniş zaman yerine geçmiş zaman fiilinin kullanıldığı bilinmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r6.claim: As the zygote's extensions attach to and hang from the uterine lining, the verse calls this suspended stage alaqa, matching the word's dictionary sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r6.anchor: hücrelerin bazı uzantılar çıkararak rahim iç zarına asılıp tutundukları ve bir iki gün bu vaziyette kaldıkları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r7.claim: The embryo becomes a shapeless flesh-like morsel, develops bones, and then muscles, vessels, and nerves are covered with flesh to complete the body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r7.anchor: zamanla kemikler oluşur, kemikler kas, damar ve sinirlerle, bunlar da etle kaplanarak insan bedeninin oluşumu tamamlanır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.claim: The passage summarizes each person's biological formation from soil-derived food and plant growth through gestation to a fully formed body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.anchor: topraktan, dolayısıyla toprakta beslenip büyüyen bitkilerden alınan besin aşamasından başlayarak ana karnında ete kemiğe bürünmesine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r9.claim: Humans have a material origin in soil yet transcend matter through God-given senses and intellect; the final creation denotes psychological and spiritual capacities and a complete, independent personality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r9.anchor: Allah’ın kendisine bağışladığı duyu, akıl gibi meleke ve özellikler sayesinde madde üstü bir yönü olan varlıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.claim: By recalling these gifts, the verses implicitly call people to recognize their Creator and fulfill their debt of gratitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.anchor: Âyette Allah’ın insanoğluna bütün bu ihsanları hatırlatılmakta ve dolaylı olarak ondan yaratıcısını tanıyıp şükran borcunu yerine getirmesi istenmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r11.claim: After recounting humanity's creation, God praises Himself as creator of the finest work; this expresses the Qur'an's high regard for humans.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r11.anchor: insanın yaratılış serüvenini özetleyen ifadelerin ardından yüce yaratıcı, “Yapıp yaratanların en güzeli olan Allah çok yücedir” buyurarak âdeta en güzel eseriyle övünmüştür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r12.claim: The plural form hālikīn shows that creation can be attributed to others; Arabs used khalq for human making or production, but Muslims later reserved it for God as an expression of devotional propriety.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r12.anchor: Araplar’ın halk kavramını, “bir şey yapma, üretme” (sun‘) anlamında insanlara nisbet ederek kullandıkları da bildirilmektedir

QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.claim: From a uniform drop, God differentiates flesh, bone, hair, nails, nerves, skin, brain, and veins, assigning each member its form and each part its known condition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.anchor: قطرة أجزاؤها متماثلة ، ونطفة أبعاضها متشاكلة ، ثم جعل بعضها لحما وبعضها عظما

QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r10.claim: Human traits also vary without limit, including hearing, sight, thought, anger, power, knowledge, will, courage, rancor, and generosity.
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r10.anchor: ثم الصفات التي للإنسان خلقها متافوتة ، من السمع والبصر والفكر والغضب والقدرة والعلم والإرادة

QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r11.speaker: التفاسير
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r11.claim: Exegetes explain the other creation as the formation of the face.

QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r12.claim: The other creation may be the life and special faculties joined in the human, including hearing, sight, reason, discernment, and individual gifts of inspiration.
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r12.anchor: ويحتمل ما تركب فيه من الحياة ، واختص به السمع والبصر والعقل والتمييز

QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r13.claim: Alternatively, God prepares people for rare states that emerge with maturity: adornment in servanthood, release from human bondage, or realization of divine attributes through effacement of awareness of human states.
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r13.anchor: وهو أن هيأهم لأحوال عزيزة يظهرها عليهم بعد بلوغهم ، إذا حصل لهم كما التمييز

QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r1.claim: After creating the heavens, earth, Throne, Kursi, Paradise, Hell, and all creatures, God uniquely praises Himself as Best Creators after describing the creation of Adam's children, distinguishing them from other creatures.
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r1.anchor: ثم لما أخبر بذلك لم يعقبه بهذا التمدح الذي ذكره بعد نعت خلقه بني آدم تخصيصا لهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r2.claim: He notes that another verse describes the human as created in the best stature.
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r2.anchor: لقد خلقنا الإنسان فى أحسن تقويم

QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r3.claim: Even if God does not call the human the best creature here, His self-praise as Best Creators is more exalted than praise of the human.
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r3.anchor: وثناؤه على نفسه وتمدحه بذلك أعز وأجل من أن يثني عليك

QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r4.claim: Since people could not yet thank or praise God while He described their stages of creation, God praised Himself on their behalf.
QUSHAYRI:v2p337/r4.anchor: ناب عنك في الثناء على نفسه ، فقال { فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين }

BURHAN:v4p436/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p436/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p436/r3.claim: The resumptive waw introduces an independent clause, not dependent in meaning or sharing a grammatical slot; it may introduce nominal or verbal clauses and prevents mistaking a clause for a single coordinated word.
BURHAN:v4p436/r3.anchor: واو الاستثناء وتسمى واو القطع والابتداء وهي التي يكون بعدها جملة غير متعلقة بما قبلها في المعنى

BURHAN:v1p93/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p93/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p93/r5.claim: Tawshīḥ is wording whose sense signals its ending, so the close can be anticipated before it is stated; the opening and close are likened to the parts supporting a sash.
BURHAN:v1p93/r5.anchor: الثالث التوشيح ويسمى به لكون نفس الكلام يدل على آخره نزل المعنى منزلة الوشاح ونزل أول الكلام وآخره منزلة العاتق والكشح

BURHAN:v1p93/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p93/r6.speaker: ابن وكيع
BURHAN:v1p93/r6.claim: Ibn Wakīʿ calls tawshīḥ al-muṭmiʿ, because the opening makes the reader anticipate its ending; the example is the creation verse.
BURHAN:v1p93/r6.anchor: وسماه ابن وكيع المطمع لأن صدره مطمع فى عجزه

BURHAN:v2p49/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p49/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p49/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says revelation does not genuinely conflict with itself or reason; because God alone creates, تخلقون means “fabricate a lie” and Jesus’s خلق means “shape” clay.
BURHAN:v2p49/r4.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر في ( التقريب ) لا يجوز

BURHAN:v1p199/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p199/r1.claim: The account says the phrase about the final creation stage in 23:14 occasioned the apostasy of ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Sarḥ: while dictating it, he claimed the wording had occurred to him and that he too was a prophet.
BURHAN:v1p199/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اكتب

BURHAN:v1p312/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r5.claim: Eloquent discourse can establish divine doctrines, as the resurrection argument after describing the stages of the human seed makes listeners feel awe and fear of God.
BURHAN:v1p312/r5.anchor: فمن يقرع سمعه هذا الكلام المعجز استشعر من روعة النفس واقشعرار الجلد ما يمكن خشية الله وعظمته من قبله

BURHAN:v1p312/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r6.claim: Eloquent language also clarifies difficult non-creedal questions; the Prophet's concise reply about resemblance answers a denial of female nocturnal emission by pointing to observed resemblance to the mother.
BURHAN:v1p312/r6.anchor: وكقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فمن أين يكون الشبه فانظر كيف أعطى فى هذه الأحرف اليسيرة الحجة على من أنكر احتلام المرأة

BURHAN:v1p312/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r7.claim: Eloquent speech can evoke compassion, aversion, appeasement, anger, courage, or fear, used in praise, blame, complaint, apology, permission, and prohibition; speaker credibility and force enhance it.
BURHAN:v1p312/r7.anchor: ومنها تمكين الانفعالات النفسانية من النفوس مثل الاستعطاف والإعراض والإرضاء والإغضاب والتشجيع والتخويف

BURHAN:v3p411/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p411/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p411/r7.claim: The stages of the human seed and development are used to make the argument for resurrection take root in people's minds.
BURHAN:v3p411/r7.anchor: وذلك بعد ذكر النطفة وتقلبها في مراتب الوجود وتطورات الخلقة

BURHAN:v3p448/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p448/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURHAN:v3p448/r1.claim: One interpretation attributed to Ibn Masud takes “the living from the dead” and its reverse as semen leaving a living man dead, then a living man emerging from dead semen.
BURHAN:v3p448/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود هي النطفة تخرج من الرجل ميتة وهو حي ويخرج الرجل منها حيا وهي ميتة

BURHAN:v3p448/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p448/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v3p448/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says “bringing out” the man from the seed describes a change of state, as when one says a well-built boy will grow into a strong man.
BURHAN:v3p448/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية في تفسيره هذه الآية إن لفظة الإخراج في تنقل النطفة حتى تكون رجلا إنما هو عبارة عن تغيير الحال

BURHAN:v3p448/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p448/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p448/r3.claim: Another possible sense is that all animals are dead before God gives them life; the author identifies this as a case of tajrid, or extraction.
BURHAN:v3p448/r3.anchor: وقد يحتمل قوله ﴿ ومخرج الميت من الحي ﴾ 1 أي الحيوان كله ميتة ثم يحييه قال وهو معنى التجريد

BURHAN:v4p295/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p295/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p295/r2.claim: In the developmental sequence, “then” can mark an interval; there are intervening stages between the stated transformations.
BURHAN:v4p295/r2.anchor: وتجىء للمهلة ك ثم كقوله تعالى ﴿ ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة

BURHAN:v4p295/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p295/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p295/r10.claim: Some grammarians take the two “then” clauses in this verse, including “We clothed the bones,” as having the sense of “then” to mark delayed stages.
BURHAN:v4p295/r10.anchor: فقيل الفاء في ﴿ فخلقنا العلقة ﴾ وفي ﴿ فكسونا ﴾ بمعنى ثم لتراخي معطوفها

SULAMI:v2p32#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p32#2/r1.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p32#2/r1.claim: Creation comprises four quarters: divinity; traces of lordship; lights of governance, will, knowledge and perception; and movement and rest, by which God formed the creature.
SULAMI:v2p32#2/r1.anchor: وقال الحسين : خلق الخلق على أربع أصول فاعتدلها على أربع أصول : الربع الأعلى : إلهية ، والربع الآخر : آثار الربوبية

SULAMI:v2p32#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p32#2/r2.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p32#2/r2.claim: God originated Adam by power and formed his descendants as described; creation manifested God's eternal name, Creator, though creatures cannot comprehend His attributes and He reveals what they can bear.
SULAMI:v2p32#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسين : فطر الأشياء بقدرته ، ودبرها بلطف صنعه فأبدأ آدم كما شاء لما شاء ، وأخرج منه ذرية

ITQAN:v3p270#4/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r4.claim: The ending ‘blessed is God, the best of creators’ is perfectly fitted to the preceding account of human creation.
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r4.anchor: فإن في هذه الفاصلة التمكين التام المناسب لما قبلها

ITQAN:v3p270#4/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r5.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Thābit reports that Muʿādh ibn Jabal supplied the verse’s final phrase before hearing the revelation finished; the Prophet laughed and said, ‘With it I ended.’
ITQAN:v3p270#4/r5.anchor: فأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق الشعبي عن زيد بن ثابت قال أملى علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

ITQAN:v2p484/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p484/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p484/r2.claim: Fāʾ marks succession, with the interval measured according to the events, as in rain making the earth green and the successive stages of embryonic creation.
ITQAN:v2p484/r2.anchor: ثانيها التعقيب وهو في كل شيء بحسبه وبذلك ينفصل عن التراخي في نحو ﴿ أنزل من السماء ماء فتصبح الأرض مخضرة ﴾ ﴿ خلقنا النطفة علقة

ITQAN:v3p242#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p242#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p242#2/r1.claim: Tajrīd extracts a second entity sharing a quality with the first to intensify that quality, as when a generous man is paired with an imagined generous companion.
ITQAN:v3p242#2/r1.anchor: هو أن ينتزع من أمر ذي صفة آخر مثله مبالغة في كمالها

ITQAN:v4p451#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r1.claim: The list concerns non-irregular readings whose different forms are represented by a single written form; examples include ملك/مالك, وعدنا/واعدنا, and others.

ITQAN:v4p451#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r3.claim: The spelling list explicitly includes the embryology phrase “the morsel bones, then clothed the bones,” among forms read with or without alif.

ITQAN:v4p451#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r4.claim: Several words written with tāʾ, including “ghayyabat al-jubb” and “fī al-ghurufāt,” have both plural and singular readings.

ITQAN:v4p451#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r5.claim: The source records further orthographic alternatives involving yāʾ, alif, or omitted letters in taqiyyah, li-ahaba, yaqḍi al-ḥaqq, and related forms.
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r5.anchor: و ( تقية ) بالياء و ( لأهب ) بالألف

ITQAN:v4p451#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r6.claim: Ṣirāṭ, baṣṭah, and the two musayṭir forms are written with ṣād alone despite variant readings.
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r6.anchor: و ( المصيطرون ) و ( مصيطر ) بالصاد لا غير

ITQAN:v4p451#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r7.claim: A single rasm can accommodate both readings even when the expected alif is absent, as with fākihūn, a sound masculine plural.
ITQAN:v4p451#2/r7.anchor: وقد تكتب الكلمة صالحة للقراءتين نحو ( فكهون )

ITQAN:v1p101/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p101/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p101/r1.claim: Reports of verses revealed in agreement with a Companion are treated as a kind of occasion of revelation; ʿUmar’s agreements are its principal example.
