ITQAN:v1p101/r1.anchor: هو في الحقيقة نوع من أسباب النزول والأصل فيه موافقات عمر وقد أفردها بالتصنيف جماعة

ITQAN:v1p101/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p101/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p101/r2.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar quotes the Prophet saying that God placed truth on ʿUmar’s tongue and heart, and revelation often followed what ʿUmar had said.
ITQAN:v1p101/r2.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله جعل الحق على لسان عمر وقلبه

ITQAN:v1p101/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p101/r7.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v1p101/r7.claim: Anas reports ʿUmar saying he uttered “Blessed is God, the best of creators” after the creation passage was revealed, and that same phrase then came down.
ITQAN:v1p101/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أنس قال قال عمر وافقت ربي أو وافقني ربي في أربع

KHATTABI:v1p69/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p69/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p69/r3.claim: The Qur’an recounts successive stages in the womb, ending in a new created form with image and spirit; this displays God’s power, subtle wisdom, and abundant mercy.
KHATTABI:v1p69/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر في آية أخرى عدد انتقالاته في الرحم من نطفة إلى علقة إلى مضغة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r3.claim: Umar says he concurred with revelation four times, including saying this phrase after hearing the account of human creation; three other concordances concerned prayer, the Prophet’s wives, and veiling.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r3.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - وافقت ربي في أربع

AKHFASH:v2p454/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p454/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p454/r1.claim: Khāliqīn means makers or craftsmen, which explains the expression aḥsanu al-khāliqīn; an unnamed poet uses khalaqa for making.
AKHFASH:v2p454/r1.anchor: وقال {أحسن الخالقين} لأن الخالقين هم الصانعون. وقال الشاعر: [من الكامل وهو الشاهد الثالث والخمسون بعد المئتين] : * وأراك تغري ماخلقت

DAMGHANI:v1p403/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r12.claim: Kasw can mean spreading over the bones the sinews, veins, flesh, and skin.
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r12.anchor: الكسوة البسط قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

DAMGHANI:v1p453/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r12.claim: Anshaʾa means to create or bring into being, including creating a new kind of being.
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r12.anchor: فوجه منها أنشأ يعني خلق قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام وأنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين يعني خلقا آخرين

DAMGHANI:v1p445/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r1.claim: Death can describe the semen before it changes into the next stage; the author compares other verses about being dead and then brought to life.
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r1.anchor: الموت حال النطفة قبل انتقالها . قوله سبحانه فى 445 سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r1.claim: Mawt is an event that ends life; mawta is one death, and mawāt or mawātān can describe death among livestock or uncultivated land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r1.anchor: الموت : حادث تزول معه الحياة . والموتة : الواحدة من الموت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r2.claim: The entry also uses mawta for a madness-like fit and names Muʾta as the place where Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib was killed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r2.anchor: ومؤته - بالهمز . أرض بها قتل جعفر

FARRA:v2p232/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p232/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p232/r1.claim: خلقًا آخر refers to the human; it may instead encompass bone, semen, and nerves as one entity.
FARRA:v2p232/r1.anchor: يذهب إلى الإنسان وإن شئت: إلى العظم والنطفة» والعصب، تجعله كالشيء الواحد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r1.claim: ʿAlaqah is one clinging clot of blood, the singular of ʿalaq.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r2.claim: A muḍghah is a small piece of flesh, named for being about the amount one can chew, as ghurfah is named for what one can scoop.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r2.anchor: و (المضغة) اللحمة الصغيرة. سميت بذلك لأنها بقدر ما يمضغ، كما قيل: غرفة، بقدر ما يغرف.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r3.claim: God makes the embryo another creation by breathing spirit into it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p296#6/r3.anchor: {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} أي خلقناه بنفخ الروح فيه خلقا آخر.

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r1.claim: Khalaqa here carries the transformational sense of jaʿala and therefore takes two objects; jaʿala can likewise carry the sense of creating and take one.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r1.anchor: التصييرية فتعدت لاثنين كما تضمن جعل معنى خلق فيتعدى لواحد

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r2.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r2.claim: The common reading has both ʿiẓām and al-ʿiẓām in the plural.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r2.anchor: قرأ العامة " عظاما " و " العظام " بالجمع فيهما

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read both occurrences in the singular.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r3.anchor: وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم " عظما " و " العظم " بالإفراد فيهما

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r4.speaker: السلمي والأعرج والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r4.claim: Al-Sulamī, al-Aʿraj, and al-Aʿmash read the first occurrence singular and the second plural.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r4.anchor: والسلمي والأعرج والأعمش بإفراد الأول وجمع الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء ومجاهد وإبراهيم ابن أبي بكر
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r5.claim: Abū Rajāʾ, Mujāhid, and Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Bakr read the first occurrence plural and the second singular.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r5.anchor: وأبو رجاء ومجاهد وإبراهيم ابن أبي بكر بجمع الأول وإفراد الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r6.claim: Plural matches the intended many bones, while singular can denote a generic class, as in “my bone.”
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r6.anchor: فالجمع على الأصل لأنه مطابق لما يراد به، والإفراد للجنس كقوله

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains singular-for-plural as unambiguous because a human has many bones.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وضع الواحد موضع الجمع لزوال اللبس لأن الإنسان ذو عظام كثيرة "

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r8.claim: The grammarians of Sībawayh’s school allow singular for plural only by poetic necessity, citing a stomach in the singular although each person has one.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r8.anchor: هذا عند سيبويه وأصحابه لا يجوز إلا في ضرورة

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r9.claim: Poetry also uses singular ʿaẓm for plural throats, supporting singular-for-plural usage.

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r10.claim: A further poetic example uses singular jilduhā for the plural hides of the exhausted animals.

SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14/r11.claim: The Qurʾānic singular samʿ likewise exemplifies a singular noun used generically for plural hearing.

SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r1.claim: Aḥsanu al-khāliqīn may be apposition to the divine name, an adjective—which is preferable because derived-form apposition is uncommon—or a predicate with an omitted subject, though ellipsis is less likely.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه بدل من الجلالة. الثاني: أنه نعت للجلالة وهو أولى مما قبله

SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects the adjective parse because the superlative remains indefinite even when annexed to a definite noun.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r2.anchor: وقد منع أبو البقاء أن يكون وصفا قال: " لأنه نكرة وإن أضيف لمعرفة

SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r3.claim: The author answers that Abū al-Baqāʾ relies on one disputed account of superlative annexation; the correct account treats it as a genuine definite annexation.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r3.anchor: وهذا بناء منه على أحد القولين في أفعل التفضيل

SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r4.claim: Al-khāliqīn means those who estimate or determine; Zuhayr’s line uses khalaqta in that sense.

SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r5.claim: The comparison’s distinguishing measure is omitted but understood from the annexed noun: best in creation or estimation, just as the object of permission is understood from its relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:23:14#2/r5.anchor: والمميز لأفعل محذوف لدلالة المضاف إليه عليه

ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r1.claim: Four forms are reported: plural عظاما/العظام, singular عظما/العظم, and both mixed combinations of singular and plural.
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r1.anchor: وتقرأ على أربعة أوجه: أحدها ما ذكرنا

ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r2.claim: Singular or plural is possible because a human has many bones; the singular can stand for the collective when context, including the flesh paired with bone, signals plurality.
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r2.anchor: والتوحيد والجمع ههنا جائزان، لأنه يعلم أن الإنسان ذو عظام

ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p8#2/r3.claim: An unnamed poet's singular عظم in في حلقكم عظم وقد شجينا means bones in your throats, illustrating a singular that denotes a plural.

ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r1.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r1.claim: One explanation of the new creation is that the child becomes male or female.
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r1.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أقوال: قيل جعل ذكرا أو أنثى

ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r2.claim: A second explanation is that the spirit is breathed into the child.

ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r3.claim: A third explanation is that hair grows on the child.

ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r4.speaker: عمر
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r4.claim: A report says Umar was with the Prophet when the verse was revealed and said the closing praise; the Prophet told Umar that God had ended the verse with those words.
ZAJJAJ:v4p9/r4.anchor: ويروى أن عمر كان عند رسول الله

ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n5/r1.claim: The new creation is a distinct creature existing independently of the mother's body.
ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n5/r1.anchor: Lit., "as another creature", i.e., existing independently of the mother's body.

ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n6/r1.claim: Tabari notes that Arabs call artisans creators; since God alone is Creator in the primary sense, ahsan al-khaliqin uses khaliq secondarily.
ASAD-NOTES:23:12#n6/r1.anchor: As Tabari points out, the Arabs apply the designation "creator" to every artisan (sani')

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r1.claim: He expects later generations and specialists in law and medicine to uncover further signs, including precise Qur’anic legal and technical word choices beyond his own literary observations.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r1.anchor: وسيجد فيه أجيالُ المستقبل من ملامح الإعجاز وإشاراته ما لم يخطر لنا على بال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r2.claim: He says the Qur’anic stages of fetal development match findings established only in the modern era and notes that this led some foreign scientists to declare Islam.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r2.anchor: ما ذكره القرآن من مراحل تطور الجنين في الرحم هي التي انتهى إليها العلمُ مما لم يكنْ معروفاً قبل هذا العصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r3.claim: The term al-ʿalaqah is scientifically precise because the developing embryo at this stage resembles a leech.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r3.anchor: فاختيار التعبير بـ (العلقة) اختيارٌ له دلالته، فإن المخلوق في هذه المرحلة أشبه شيء بالعلقة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r4.speaker: كتب التفسير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r4.claim: The tafsir books define a muḍghah as a piece of flesh about the size a person can chew.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r4.anchor: فالمضغة كما قرأنا في كتب التفسير، هي القطعة من اللحم قدر ما يمضغ الماضغ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r5.claim: He adds that muḍghah specifically means flesh chewed by teeth; the embryo resembles such a piece, making the Qur’anic word choice scientifically precise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p6/r5.anchor: ذلك أن (المضغة) هي قطعة اللحم الممضوغة أي التي مضغتها الأسنان، وقد أثبت العلمُ الحديث أن الجنين في هذه المرحلة ليس قطعة لحم عادية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r1.claim: The stages of human creation culminating in a new creation make resurrection plainly possible, so it needs little further emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r1.anchor: أكبر دليل على أن إعادته ممكنة ليس في ذلك أدنى ريب، فلا يحتاج بعد هذه الأدلة إلى كبير توكيد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r2.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r2.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī explains that prior description of human creation through wondrous stages already establishes God's wisdom and power, so resurrection needs less emphasis than death.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r2.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "ولم يؤكد سبحانه أمرَ البعث تأكيده لأمر الموت مع كثرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r4.claim: In human reasoning, re-creating what was first made is easier than originating it: the first creation receives lām and qad, while resurrection receives only inna; for God, nothing is easier than anything else.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p117/r4.anchor: إن الإعادة أسهل من الابتداء في منطق العقل، فإن الذي يصنع كل يوم آلاف النماذج

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r1.claim: The perfected, wondrous creation can suggest that humanity was made to endure, making the announcement of death after all that seem unexpected and warranting its emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r1.anchor: إن ما ذكره الله من خلق الإنسانه وتطويره حتى صار مخلوقاً على أحسن هيئة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r2.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r2.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī says the preceding stress on God's precise creation makes death so counterintuitive that an unobservant listener might almost deny it, explaining the extra emphasis on mortality.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p118/r2.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "ولما تضمنت الجملة السابقة المبالغة في أنه تعالى شأنه أحكم خلق الإنسان وأتقنه،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r3.claim: خلق can mean bringing something into existence from nothing, which belongs to God, or shaping something, which people can also do.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r3.anchor: الخلق في اللغة لها معنيان: الخلق ابتداء أي إيجاد من العدم وهذا خاص بالله سبحانه وتعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r4.claim: أحسن الخالقين is apt because الخلق also means shaping; Jesus’s statement about making a bird’s form from clay illustrates that nondivine sense.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r4.anchor: (أحسن الخالقين) يصح أن تكون لأنها ليست خاصة بالإيجاد من العدم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r5.claim: The author also cites al-Hajjaj’s phrase ولا أخلق إلا فريق as an example of خلق used beyond divine creation from nothing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r5.anchor: وفي خطية الحجاج قال (ولا أخلق إلا فريق)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.claim: Emphasis depends on context: al-Mu’minūn mentions death more often and foregrounds human creation, so creation receives two emphases and resurrection one, since resurrection is easier than originating life; both are easy for God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.anchor: فلهذا جعل سبحانه وتعالى توكيدين في الخلق وتوكيداً واحداً في البعث لأن البعث أهون عليه من الخلق من عدم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.claim: He says the Qur’anic account of embryonic stages matches knowledge reached only in the modern era, which specialists in anatomy and medicine describe as scientifically precise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.anchor: مما لم يكن معروفاً قبل هذا العصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r2.claim: The term ʿalaqah is apt because the developing creature at that stage most resembles the known parasitic leech.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r2.anchor: المخلوق في هذه المرحلة أشبه شيء بالعلقة وهي الطفيلية المعروفة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r3.claim: A muḍghah is chewed flesh; he says modern science shows the embryo at this stage resembles meat chewed by teeth, making the term more precise than a generic small piece of flesh.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r3.anchor: أن الجنين في هذه المرحلة ليس قطعة لحم عادية بل هو كقطعة اللحم التي مضغتها الأسنان

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.claim: The preceding believers' glad tidings and the warnings implicit for faithless disbelievers are realities, though deniers of resurrection and the hereafter dismiss them as fantasy and mock them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.anchor: The glad tidings given to the believers in the previous section are a definite reality. Similarly, the warnings they conceal for the disbelievers devoid of faith are also a definite reality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.claim: People who reject resurrection and the hereafter treat the promised realities as imaginary and make fun of them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.anchor: By presenting the objections of such people, attention is directed to the signs in their inside and outside world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.claim: Reflection on the stages of human creation makes clear that the God who created people can readily recreate those who die and decay into dust.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.anchor: if a person only reflects on the phases of his creation it will become crystal clear that the God Who is capable of doing all this can have no difficulty in re-creating those who die and decay into dust.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.claim: The resurrection argument also appears in 22:5; this passage develops it further and elaborates aspects not treated there.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.anchor: This argument has also been stated in verse 5 of S ūrah al-Ḥajj.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.claim: Islahi connects the creation stages here with 22:5: there they prove resurrection, and “so that We make evident for you” signals that the gradual sequence displays God's power and wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.anchor: There, the opening words were: ﺐٍ رَﻳۡ ﺘﻢۡ /.ۡ ﻛﻨۡ نۡ ﻣ	ﻦَ  ﻟۡﺒَﻌۡﺚ if you are in any doubt of being raised to life again

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.claim: The stages of human development are familiar, and modern science has disclosed aspects the Qur'an only hinted at; further knowledge reveals more of these secrets.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.anchor: the more knowledge human beings gain, the more they know of these secrets.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.claim: A drop arising from clay is gradually nourished until it becomes people such as Socrates, Hippocrates, Aristotle, and Galen, prompting reflection on whether this elaborate process is accidental.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.anchor: ultimately, the likes of Socrates, Hippocrates, Aristotle and Galen are created. The question is: Is all this happening of its own accord?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.claim: The sequence of creation, its care, and its evident power and wisdom cannot be meaningless products of uncontrolled matter; the One who forms a human from a drop can recreate that person.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.anchor: Is all this power, wisdom, providence and affection a meaningless thing which has no purpose and fate? Is the being Who fashions out a human being from a drop of fluid unable to create him again?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.claim: The Qur'an directs people to inspect their own bodies and stages of development; reflection there supplies the answers without searching far afield.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.anchor: If they reflect on their own phases of creation, they will get all the answers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r2.claim: “A new creation altogether” points to the astonishing transformation from a fluid drop into a living human, making denial of the Creator's power to resurrect unreasonable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r2.anchor: The words “then We made it into a new creation altogether” point to the incredible nature of transformation a drop of fluid undergoes to become a living human being.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r3.claim: The stages of creation should lead a reflective person to recognize God as blessed and beneficent: He turns an ordinary drop into a miraculous human endowed with extraordinary capacities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r3.anchor: The God Who showed His signs, marvels and miracles in every person is blessed and beneficent

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r4.claim: Humanity's remarkable stature is illustrated by the angels bowing to Adam and humans becoming God's vicegerents on earth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r4.anchor: such are his abilities that angels bowed down to him and he became the vicegerent of God on earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r5.claim: Reflection should establish not only God's existence but that the Creator is wise, beneficent, powerful, blessed, and peerless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r5.anchor: a person does not merely acknowledge the existence of God, he is convinced that his creator is wise, beneficent, powerful, blessed and peerless.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r6.claim: The superlative afʿal, especially when annexed to a plural noun, can magnify an attribute rather than compare; “best of creators” means the Creator fashioned humans in the best mould with the best abilities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r6.anchor: the superlative أﻓﻌﻞespecially when annexed to a plural noun, at times does not signify any comparison

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r7.claim: Some exegetes alter the sense of “creator” because they miss this Arabic usage; Islahi rejects that change as unnecessary.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r7.anchor: Some exegetes have changed the meaning of the word “creator” because of not being aware of this style. Obviously, this is not the slightest needed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r8.claim: Human creation refutes accounts based on uncontrolled matter, a prime mover, a first cause, or self-evolution; a blessed, outstanding Creator brought humanity into being.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r8.anchor: he has not been created by matter that is unbridled or by a prime mover or by a first cause nor has he evolved on its own.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r1.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r1.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim and Ibn Amir read the bone noun singular in both places; the others, including Hafs, read it plural.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r1.anchor: فقرأ عاصم وحده في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر: (عظما فكسونا العظم لحما) واحدا ليس قبل الميم ألف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r2.speaker: الباقون وحفص عن عاصم وبكار عن أبان عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r2.claim: The remaining readers, including Hafs and Bakkar's transmission, read عظاما and العظام in the plural.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وحفص عن عاصم وبكار عن أبان عن عاصم: عظاما فكسونا العظام لحما جماعا بألف .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r3.claim: The plural better matches the Quran's other descriptions of bones; the singular remains possible as a generic collective noun.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r3.anchor: والجمع أشبه بما جاء في التنزيل في غير هذا الموضع كقوله: أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r4.claim: The singular is a generic noun like الإنسان, الدرهم, الشاء, and البعير, not the idiomatic singular in كلوا في بعض بطنكم تعفوا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r4.anchor: والإفراد أنه اسم جنس، وأفرد كما تفرد المصادر وغيرها من الأجناس نحو: الإنسان والدرهم والشاء والبعير

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r5.claim: Abu Zayd's verse uses القراد as a singular collective for many ticks, supporting the generic singular reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p288/r5.anchor: فالقراد يراد به الكثرة لا محالة.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r1.speaker: السلمي وقتادة والأعرج والأعمش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r1.claim: Al-Sulamī, Qatāda, al-Aʿraj, and al-Aʿmash read bone first in the singular, then bones in the plural; the source says reports differ among them.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r1.anchor: جماعة -السلمي وقتادة والأعرج والأعمش. واختلف عنهم.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r2.claim: Mujāhid reads bones first in the plural, then bone in the singular.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p87/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī prefers singular then plural: the singular matches the preceding human and embryonic nouns, then shifts to the intended generality; poetry uses singular collectively, as in an unnamed poet’s بطنكم and Ṭufayl’s عظم, while returning to singular after a plural shift is less apt.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p256/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p256/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p256/r1.claim: “We clothed the bones with flesh” is read with singular or plural “bones,” as discussed for “their prayers.”
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p256/r1.anchor: يقرأبالتوحيد والجمع على ما ذكرنا في قوله

NASHR:v2p328/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p328/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
NASHR:v2p328/r4.claim: Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read both occurrences of bone in the singular; the other readers read both in the plural.
NASHR:v2p328/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر (عظما) و (العظم) بفتح العين

QIRAAT-ER:23:14:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:14:12#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:23:14:12#1/r1.claim: The singular ʿaẓman treats bone as substance or material, while plural ʿiẓāman presents the bones as a system.
QIRAAT-ER:23:14:12#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: singular ʿaẓman instead of plural ʿiẓāman — shifts from ""bones"" (system) to ""bone"" (substance/material)

QIRAAT-ER:23:14:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:14:15#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:23:14:15#1/r1.claim: Singular al-ʿaẓma describes bone as substance rather than plural al-ʿiẓāma as a system of bones.
QIRAAT-ER:23:14:15#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: singular al-ʿaẓma instead of plural al-ʿiẓāma — ""the bone"" as substance rather than ""the bones"" as system

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r1.claim: One reported view identifies the creation of another form as the growth of hair.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر ﴾ قال يقول بعضهم هو نبات الشعر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r2.claim: A different reported view identifies the creation of another form as the breathing of the spirit.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r2.anchor: قال يقول بعضهم هو نبات الشعر ويقول بعضهم هو نفخ الروح

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r3.claim: The reading attributed to Ibn Masʿūd has “then We brought forth for him another creation.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p44#5/r3.anchor: قال قتادة وفي حرف ابن مسعود ثم أنشأنا له خلقا آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r1.claim: ʿAlaqa is congealed blood, formed when qualities accrue to the blood and change its description; this is qualitative motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r1.anchor: أي دما جامدا وذلك بإضافة أعراض الدم عليها فتصيرها دما بحسب الوصف وهذا من باب الحركة في الكيف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r2.claim: Mudgha is a chew-sized piece of flesh without clear differentiation; its formation from ʿalaqa is a change in substance, like water becoming stone, as one form leaves matter and another enters.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r2.anchor: أي قطعة لحم بقدر ما يمضغ لا استبانة ولا تمايز فيها وهذا التصيير على ما قيل بحسب الذات

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r3.claim: The substantial change involves gradual shifts in readiness: matter loses its disposition for the prior form and gains one for the next until the earlier form vanishes and the new one occurs at once.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r3.anchor: ولا يزال الأول ينقص والثاني يشتد إلى أن تنتهي المادة إلى حيث تزول عنها الصورة الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r4.claim: The lump becomes bones—small and large as wisdom requires—through hardening the parts intended for bone; this is a qualitative change.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r4.anchor: وهذا أيضا تصيير بحسب الوصف فيكون من الباب الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r5.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r5.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī's account implies that nuṭfa and ʿalaqa, and likewise mudgha and bone, share an underlying reality differing in qualities; ʿalaqa and mudgha differ in essence as well as qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r5.anchor: وفي كلام العلامة البيضاوي إشارة ما إلى مجموع ما ذكرنا وهو يستلزم القول بأن النطفة والعلقة متحدان في الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r6.claim: The author accepts that successive forms occur in one underlying matter throughout the stages until the human form, unless evidence establishes otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r6.anchor: والظاهر أنه تتعاقب في جميع هذه الأطوار على مادة واحدة صور حسب تعاقب الاستعدادات

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r7.claim: Covering the bones with flesh is like clothing them; the flesh may be leftover from the part of the lump not made bone, or fresh flesh God creates from blood in the womb.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13#2/r7.anchor: أي جعلناه ساترا لكل منها كاللباس وذلك اللحم يحتمل أن يكون من لحم المضغة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r1.claim: Bones are singled out because their shapes and hardness vary unlike the other parts; the source reports a count of 248 bones according to some.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r1.anchor: دون غيرها مما في الأطوار لأنها متغايرة هيئة وصلابة بخلاف غيرها ألا ترى عظم الساق

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وأبان والمفضل والحسن وقتادة وهارون والجعفي ويونس عن أبي عمرو وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r2.claim: They read “bone” in the singular at both occurrences, using a collective singular for few or many without ambiguity; the singular also matches the preceding stages.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم وأبان والمفضل والحسن وقتادة وهارون والجعفي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r3.claim: The singular collective construction is not necessarily restricted to poetic or forced usage despite a claim attributed to Sībawayh; the cited Arabic verse says “eat within part of your belly and you will be healthy.”
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r3.anchor: كما في قوله + كلوا في بعض بطنكم تعفوا + واختصاص مثل ذلك بالضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r4.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r4.claim: Ibn Jinnī notes that singular “bone” here creates parallelism with the singular forms used for the earlier developmental stages.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14/r4.anchor: وفي الإفراد هنا مشاكلة لما ذكر قبل في الأطوار كما ذكره ابن جني

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.speaker: السلمي وقتادة والأعرج والأعمش ومجاهد وابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.claim: These readers make the first occurrence of bone singular and the second plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r1.anchor: قرأ السلمي وقتادة أيضا والأعرج والأعمش ومجاهد وابن محيصن بإفراد الأول وجمع الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء وإبراهيم بن أبي بكر ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.claim: These readers reverse the pattern, making the first occurrence plural and the second singular.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء وإبراهيم بن أبي بكر ومجاهد أيضا بجمع الأول وإفراد الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.claim: The later creation is radically unlike the earlier stages: a rational, speaking, hearing, seeing animal containing wonders in every limb and part.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r3.anchor: مباينا للخلق الأول مباينة ما أبعدها حيث جعل حيوانا ناطقا سميعا بصيرا وأودع كل عضو

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r4.claim: A verse likens the seemingly small human body to a microcosm containing the greater world.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r4.anchor: ومن هنا قيل : وتزعم أنك جرم صغير وفيك انطوى العالم الأكبر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.claim: Another creation is the spirit, understood as the rational soul; the phrase can mean that it was created for or within the body.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r5.anchor: وقيل الخلق الآخر الروح والمراد بها النفس الناطقة والمعنى أنشأنا له أو فيه خلقا آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.claim: The apparent temporal force of then indicates that the spirit was created after the body; most Islamic theologians and Aristotle hold this.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r6.anchor: وظاهر العطف بثم يقتضي حدوثها بعد حدوث البدن وهو قول أكثر الإسلاميين وإليه ذهب أرسطو

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r7.speaker: بعض المسلمين
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r7.claim: Some explain the spirit's creation as attachment to the body, while most Muslims understand it as permeating the body.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r7.anchor: وهو عند بعض عبارة عن جعلها متعلقة به وعند أكثر المسلمين جعلها سارية فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.claim: If the reference is to the animal spirit, it plainly arises after the body and permeates it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r8.anchor: وإذا أريد بالروح الروح الحيوانية فلا كلام في حدوثها بعد البدن وسريانها فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r9.claim: A reported alternative identifies the later creation as the sensory faculties.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r10.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the later creation is teeth and hair; when challenged that babies may have hair at birth, he points to pubic and armpit hair, a claim the author derides.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r10.anchor: وقال الضحاك ويكاد يضحك منه فيما أخرجه عنه عبد بن حميد : الخلق الآخر الأسنان والشعر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r11.claim: Then usually marks temporal sequence, but may instead mark rank because this second creation is greater and higher than the earlier stages.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r11.anchor: هو ما يقتضيه أكثر استعمالاتها ويجوز أن نكون للترتيب الرتبي فإن الخلق الثاني أعظم من الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r12.claim: Alternating then and fa signals differing degrees of remoteness between transformations; stages marked then are more surprising than transitions marked fa.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r12.anchor: للإشارة إلى تفاوت الإستحالات فالمعطوف بثم مستبعد حصوله مما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r13.claim: The transformations include the lump hardening into bone and being covered with flesh; the author says this account remains debatable.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r13.anchor: وكذا تصليب المضغة حتى تصير عظما وكذا مد لحمها عليه ليستره كذا قيل ولا يخلو عن قيل وقال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r14.claim: Abu Hanifa infers that one who usurps an egg that hatches owes for the egg, not the chick, because it is a new creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r14.anchor: واستدل الإمام أبو حنيفة بقوله تعالى ( ثم أنشأناه ) الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r15.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r15.claim: Al-Kashf objects that the chick's distinctness as a new creation does not remove it from the owner's property under opponents' principles.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r15.anchor: قال في الكشف : وفي هذا الإستدلال نظر على أصل مخالفيه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r16.speaker: صاحب التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r16.claim: Al-Taqrib says the chick is compensable because it is part of the usurped property, not because it is identical to or named as the egg.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r16.anchor: وقال صاحب التقريب : إن تضمينه للفرخ لكونه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r17.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r17.claim: The Imam argues that the verse refutes al-Nazzam's claim that humans are only spirit and philosophers' claim that humans are indivisible and not bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r17.anchor: قال الإمام : قالوا في الآية دلالة على بطلان قول النظام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r18.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r18.claim: The philosophers identify the human with the rational soul, an immaterial spirit neither divisible nor inside or outside the body.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r18.anchor: وكأنهم أرادوا أن الإنسان هو النفس الناطقة والروح الأمرية المجردة فإنها التي ليست بجسم عندهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r19.claim: Tabaraka declares God exalted and sanctified in His encompassing knowledge and overwhelming power.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r19.anchor: فتعالى وتقدس شأنه سبحانه في علمه الشامل وقدرته الباهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r20.claim: Tabaraka is a past-tense verb that does not inflect for other forms; it is most often attributed to a non-feminine subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r20.anchor: تبارك ) فعل ماض لا يتصرف والأكثر إسناده إلى غير مؤنث

ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r21.claim: The shift to the majestic name instills awe, marks the wondrous acts as divine prerogatives, and invites hearers to glorify God.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p14#2/r21.anchor: والإلتفات إلى الإسم الجليل لتربية المهابة وإدخال الروعة والإشعار بأن ما ذكر من الأفاعيل العجيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r1.claim: The preferred parsing makes best of creators an adjective of the majestic name; the definite superlative construction itself conveys definiteness.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r1.anchor: نعت للإسم الجليل وإضافة أفعل التفضيل محضة فتفيده تعريفا إذا أضيف إلى معرفة على الأصح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa denies that the phrase is an adjective because the superlative remains indefinite, and proposes rare apposition or a predicate with an omitted pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : لا يجوز أن يكون نعتا لأنه نكرة وإن أضيف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r3.claim: The superlative's distinguishing noun, creation, is omitted because creators already indicates it; goodness describes the act of creating.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r3.anchor: أي أحسن الخالقين خلقا فالحسن للخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r4.claim: The author compares the ellipsis to the hadith that God is beautiful and loves beauty, understood to mean that His action is beautiful.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r4.anchor: قيل : نظيره قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى جميل يحب الجمال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r5.claim: The root kh-l-q can mean measuring or determining, and may describe human action, as shown by a verse about shaping a bird from clay and a line by Zuhayr.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r5.anchor: والخلق بمعنى التقدير وهو وصف يطلق على غيره تعالى كما في قوله تعالى ( وإذ نخلق من الطين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya interprets creation as making or crafting.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r6.anchor: وفي معنى ذلك تفسيره بالصنع كما فعل ابن عطية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r7.claim: Creation meaning bringing into existence belongs only to God; attributing it to another is possible only hypothetically.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r7.anchor: ولا يصح تفسيره بالإيجاد عندنا إذ لا خالق بذلك المعنى غيره تعالى إلا أن يكون على الفرض والتقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r8.claim: The Mu'tazila interpret creator as one who brings things into existence because they believe humans independently create their actions.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p15/r8.anchor: والمعتزلة يفسرونه بذلك لقولهم بأن العبد خالق لأفعاله وموجد لها استقلالا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r1.claim: God's good creation means that He makes it precise and perfect.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r1.anchor: ومعنى حسن خلقه تعالى اتقانه وإحكامه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r2.claim: Alternatively, goodness contrasts with ugliness: everything from God is good insofar as it comes from Him, so the verse does not prove that He does not create unbelief and sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r2.anchor: وكل شيء منه عز وجل شأنه حسن لا يتصف بالقبح أصلا من حيث أنه منه فلا دليل فيه للمعتزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet's scribe Abd Allah b. Sa'd uttered the closing glorification before it was dictated; the Prophet said it was revealed that way and Ibn Sa'd apostatized.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r3.anchor: روي أن عبد الله بن سعيد بن أبي سرح كان يكتب لرسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r4.claim: The account says Ibn Sa'd later returned to Islam before death and did well; another report says he died an unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r4.anchor: ثم أسلم قبل وفاته عليه الصلاة والسلام وحسن إسلامه وقيل : مات كافرا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r5.claim: Critics object that the report implies a Medinan apostasy although the sura is Meccan; reconciliation is possible if this verse was dictated in Medina or itself Medinan.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r5.anchor: بأن السورة مكية وارتداده كما تقتضيه الرواية وأجيب بأنه يمكن الجمع بأن تكون الآية نازلة بمكة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r6.claim: If this verse is Medinan, al-Suyuti's exception of only 23:64–77 from the Meccan sura is incomplete.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون اقتصار الجلال السيوطي على استثناء قوله تعالى ( حتى أخذنا مترفيهم ) إلى قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r7.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r7.claim: A report from Zayd b. Thabit says Muadh supplied the closing words while the Prophet dictated; the Prophet laughed and said that was how it ended.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r7.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : أملى علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r8.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Umar supplied the closing words as the verse was revealed; Anas says Umar counted it among four divine agreements.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r8.anchor: قال عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه : ( فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين ) فنزلت كما قال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r9.claim: The Qur'an's composition is so strong that beginnings of many verses disclose their endings; poetry likewise praises verses whose openings reveal their rhymes.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r9.anchor: من حسن نظم القرآن الكريم حيث تدل صدور كثير من آياته على إعجازها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r10.claim: Human beings anticipating Qur'anic wording does not disprove its inimitability, measured against a passage as short as the shortest sura.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r10.anchor: لا يقال : فقد تكلم البشر ابتداء بمثل نظم القرآن الكريم وذلك قادح في إعجازه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r11.claim: This verse's inimitability depends on the preceding passage; its fa introduces a concluding interjection confirming what came before.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p16/r11.anchor: أن إعجاز هذه الآية الكريمة منوط بما قبلها كما تعرب عنه الفاء اعتراض تذييلي مقرر لمضمون ما قبله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read the two bone references in the singular; the other readers use the plural because a person has many bones.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر "عظما"، {فكسونا العظام} على التوحيد فيهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r2.claim: One view says forty days separate each of the stages of creation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r2.anchor: وقيل: بين كل خلقين أربعون يوما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r3.claim: God clothed the bones with flesh.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والشعبي وعكرمة والضحاك وأبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Shaʿbī, ʿIkrimah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Abū al-ʿĀliyah say the new creation is the breathing of the spirit into the person.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ومجاهد، والشعبي، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو العالية: هو نفخ الروح فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r5.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r5.claim: Qatādah identifies the new creation as the growth of teeth and hair.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r6.claim: In a report through Ibn Jurayj, Mujāhid says the phrase means reaching full youth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r6.anchor: وروى ابن جريج عن مجاهد: أنه استواء الشباب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r7.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the new creation means becoming male or female.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن قال: ذكرا أو أنثى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r8.claim: Al-ʿAwfī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the phrase covers life’s changing states after birth, from first cry and nursing through movement, weaning, maturity, and later stages.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412/r8.anchor: وروى العوفي عن ابن عباس: أن ذلك تصريف أحواله بعد الولادة من الاستهلال إلى الارتضاع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r1.claim: God deserves exaltation and praise, as He always has and always will.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r1.anchor: {فتبارك الله} أي: استحق التعظيم والثناء بأنه لم يزل ولا يزال.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r2.claim: Aḥsan al-khāliqīn means best of image-makers and estimators; in Arabic, khalq means estimation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r2.anchor: {أحسن الخالقين} المصورين والمقدرين. و"الخلق" في اللغة: التقدير.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says people make things and God makes things, but God is the best maker; khāliq can mean maker.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يصنعون ويصنع الله والله خير الصانعين، يقال: رجل خالق أي: صانع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the plural “creators” by noting that Jesus also creates, as stated in Āl ʿImrān 3:49; God is the best of creators.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p412#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: إنما جمع الخالقين لأن عيسى كان يخلق كما قال: "إني أخلق لكم من الطين" (آل عمران -49)

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r3.claim: The white semen becomes a red clot, then a piece of flesh, then bones made hard.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r3.anchor: بأن أحلنا النطفة البيضاء علقة حمراء. { فخلقنا العلقة مضغة } فصيرناها قطعة لحم. { فخلقنا المضغة عظما } بأن صلبناها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r4.claim: The flesh comes from the remainder of the morsel or from what grows onto bones from nourishment reaching them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r4.anchor: مما بقي من المضغة أو مما أنبتنا عليها مما يصل إليها، واختلاف العواطف لتفاوت الاستحالات

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r5.claim: Conjunctions vary because transformations differ; plurals reflect differences in form and hardness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r5.anchor: واختلاف العواطف لتفاوت الاستحالات والجمع لاختلافها في الهيئة والصلابة

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read both terms in the singular, using a generic singular in place of the plural; another reading makes one singular and the other plural.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر على التوحيد فيهما اكتفاء باسم الجنس عن الجمع، وقرىء بإفراد أحدهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r7.claim: The new creation may be bodily form, spirit, faculties created by breathing the spirit into it, or all together.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r7.anchor: وهو صورة البدن أو الروح أو القوى بنفخه فيه أو المجموع

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r8.claim: “Then” marks the great difference between the two stages of creation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r8.anchor: ثم } لما بين الخلقين من التفاوت، واحتج به أبو حنيفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa used this to argue that one who usurps an egg that hatches in his possession owes the egg, not the chick, because it becomes a different creation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r9.anchor: واحتج به أبو حنيفة على أن من غصب بيضة أفرخت عنده لزمه ضمان البيضة لا الفرخ

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r10.claim: God’s exalted station is manifested in His power and wisdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r10.anchor: فتبارك الله } فتعالى شأنه في قدرته وحكمته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r11.claim: “Best of creators” means best of estimators; the distinguishing noun is omitted because الخالقين makes it understood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r11.anchor: المقدرين تقديرا فحذف المميز لدلالة { الخلقين } عليه.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r1.claim: The first transformation is extraordinary and the drop may either spoil or begin developing, so the author uses creation and thumma to mark delay and elevated rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r1.anchor: ولما كان تصيير الماء دما أمرا بالغا خارجا عن التسبيب , وكانت النطفة التي هي مبدأ الآدمي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r2.claim: The drop is very white; the ʿalaqa is thick, coagulated, intensely red blood.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r2.anchor: النطفة } أي البيضاء جدا { علقة } حمراء دما عبيطا شديد الحمرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r3.claim: From the clot onward, each ascending stage follows its predecessor without delay by God's unique decree, not through a process available to others; fa marks this succession.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r3.anchor: ولما كان ما بعد العلقة من الأطوار المتصاعدة مسببا كل واحد منه عما قبله بتقدير العزيز العليم الذي اختص به من غير تراخ

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r4.claim: A mudgha is a small piece of flesh without shape or pattern.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r4.anchor: مضغة } أي قطعة لحم صغيرة لا شكل فيها ولا تخطيط

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r5.claim: God refines and hardens the flesh through heat and subtle processes to form bones of the head, feet, and everything between.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r5.anchor: بتصفيتها وتصلبيها بما سببنا لها من الحرارة والأمور اللطيفة الغامضة { عظاما } من رأس ورجلين وما بينهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r6.claim: God clothes the bones with flesh, covering, strengthening, and binding them with ligaments and nerves.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r6.anchor: فسترنا تلك العظام وقويناها وشددناها بالروابط والأعصاب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r7.claim: The final creation refers to forming the human and breathing in the spirit, producing a living, speaking, articulate person far removed from clay.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r7.anchor: { ثم أنشأناه } أي هذا المحدث عنه بعظمتنا { خلقا آخر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r8.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r8.claim: Al-Razi says the root letters nūn-shīn-hamza indicate the elevation and loftiness of something.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p187/r8.anchor: قال الرازي : وأصل النون والشين والهمزة يدل على ارتفاع شيء وسموه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r1.claim: God is permanently established in every perfection and free of every defect; any incapacity would contradict that complete perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r1.anchor: ثبت ثباتا لم يثبته شيء , بأن حاز جميع صفات الكمال , وتنزه عن كل شائبة نقص

BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r2.claim: The proper name Allah gathers all the beautiful names and their meanings.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r2.anchor: فعبر بالاسم العلم الجامع لجميع الأسماء الحسنى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r3.claim: Khāliqīn here means those who measure or determine; God best determines this wondrous creation and guides it through every human life stage.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r3.anchor: أي المقدرين , أي قدر هذا الخلق العجيب هذا التقدير , ثم طوره في أطواره ما بين طفل رضيع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r4.claim: Human development ranges from infancy through adolescence, vigorous youth, adulthood, and old age, with innumerable states known only to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p188/r4.anchor: ما بين طفل رضيع , ومحتلم شديد , وشاب نشيط , وكهل عظيم , وشيخ هرم

ABUDAWUD:760/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:760/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUDAWUD:760/r1.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet used the verse’s concluding praise while prostrating, within a supplication that glorifies God as the best of creators.

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r8.claim: Asked about withdrawal, Ibn Abbas rejects calling it minor infanticide before the embryo passes through the stages recited in the creation passage.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: سألنا ابن عباس عن العزل فقال: اذهبوا فاسألوا الناس ثم ائتوني واخبروني

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have recited the phrase with the morsel becoming bones.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن أنه كان يقرأ {فخلقنا المضغة عظاما}

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r12.claim: Qatada is reported to have recited the phrase with the morsel becoming bones, followed by covering the bones with flesh.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r12.anchor: عن قتادة أنه كان يقرأ {فخلقنا المضغة عظاما فكسونا العظام لحما}

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r13.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r13.claim: Asim recited ʿaẓman without the alif and treated the following al-ʿizam as singular.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r13.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ (فخلقنا المضغة عظما) بغير ألف (فكسونا العظام) على واحده

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the further creation as breathing the spirit into the embryo.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} قال: نفخ فيه الروح

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r15.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r15.claim: Abu al-Aliya likewise interprets the further creation as the spirit being placed in the human.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r15.anchor: عن أبي العالية {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} قال: جعل فيه الروح

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r1.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r1.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima are reported to give the same interpretation as Abu al-Aliya: the further creation is the spirit being placed in the human.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r1.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن مجاهد وعكرمة مثله

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r2.claim: Mujahid says the further creation occurs when the human reaches youth.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} قال: حين استوى به الشباب

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the further creation is teeth and hair; answering that some are born with hair, he asks where their pubic and armpit hair is.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} قال: الأسنان والشعر قيل أليس قد يولد وعلى رأسه الشعر

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r4.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r4.claim: Salih Abu al-Khalil reports that Umar said the verse's closing words at revelation; the Prophet said the passage ended as Umar had said.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r4.anchor: قال عمر {فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين} فقال والذي نفسي بيده إنها ختمت بالذي تكلمت يا عمر

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r5.speaker: عزير
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r5.claim: Wahb transmits Uzayr's account that God made seven heavens from water in the air and separated earth from water into lands and seas.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r5.anchor: قال عزير: يا رب أمرت الماء فجمد في وسط الهواء فجعلت منه سبعا

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r6.speaker: عزير
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r6.claim: Wahb transmits Uzayr's account that God created varied animals from water, gave them different bodies and senses, and made diverse kinds and pairs.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r6.anchor: خلقت من الماء أعمى عين بصرته ومنها أصم آذان أسمعته ومنها ميت أنفس أحييته

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r7.speaker: عزير
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r7.claim: Uzayr says God made plants from one word, one earth, and one water, yet their tastes, colors, scents, and qualities vary widely.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r7.anchor: وقال عزير: اللهم بكلمتك خلقت جميع خلقك فأتى على مشيئتك ثم زرعت في أرضك كل نبات فيها بكلمة واحدة

DURR-FULL:v6p92/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r8.speaker: عزير
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r8.claim: Uzayr describes human bodies formed in their mothers' wombs and shaped with limbs, bones, senses, and provisions.
DURR-FULL:v6p92/r8.anchor: وقال عزير: يا رب إنما نحن خلقك وعمل يديك خلقت أجسادنا في أرحام أمهاتنا وصورتنا كيف تشاء

DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r1.speaker: عزير
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r1.claim: Uzayr continues describing bodies formed in the womb, with bones, senses, light, space, and breath, and nourishment prepared without effort.
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r1.anchor: جعلت لنا أركانا وجعلت فيها عظاما وفتقت لنا أسماعا وأبصارا ثم جعلت لنا في تلك الظلمة نورا

DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r2.speaker: عزير
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r2.claim: Uzayr says that before the ordered alternation of night and day, God's Throne was on water, darkness in the air, and angels carried the Throne while creation obeyed.
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r2.anchor: كان عرشك على الماء والظلمة على الهواء والملائكة يحملون عرشك ويسبحون بحمدك والخلق مطيع لك

DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r3.speaker: عزير
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r3.claim: Uzayr says God opened the storehouse of light and path of darkness, making night and day alternate by divine command.
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r3.anchor: ثم فتحت خزانة النور وطريق الظلمة فكانا ليلا ونهارا يختلفنا بأمرك

DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r4.claim: Wahb says God made Adam from clay and water, then gave him bodily nature and senses and a spirit enabling moral discernment and planning.
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r4.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: خلق الله آدم كما شاء ومما شاء فكان كذلك {فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين}

DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r5.claim: Wahb's account explains human health through four humors: balanced quarters make a sound body, while excess or deficiency of any one causes illness.
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r5.anchor: ثم جعلت فيه من هذه الفطر الأربع أنواعا من الخلق أربعة في جسد ابن آدم فهي قوام جسده وملاكه بإذن الله

DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r6.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r6.claim: Ali says that after four months in the womb, an angel is sent to breathe the spirit into the embryo in the three darknesses; this is the further creation.
DURR-FULL:v6p92#2/r6.anchor: عن علي قال: إذا نمت النطفة أربعة أشهر بعث إليها ملك فنفخ فيها الروح في الظلمات الثلاث

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas traces the new creation after birth through crying, feeding, sitting, crawling, walking, weaning, eating, puberty and maturity.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس في قوله {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} يقول: خرج من بطن أمه

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r2.speaker: بعضهم عن قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r2.claim: Qatada reports one view that the new creation means the growth of hair.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وابن جرير عن قتادة {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} قال: يقول بعضهم هو نبات الشعر

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r3.speaker: بعضهم عن قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r3.claim: Qatada reports another view that the new creation means the spirit being breathed into the body.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر} قال: يقول بعضهم هو نبات الشعر وبعضهم يقول: هو نفخ الروح

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r4.claim: Mujahid says people make things, while God is the best maker.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن مجاهد {فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين} قال: يصنعون ويصنع الله والله خير الصانعين

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Jesus son of Mary creates.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن جريج {فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين} قال: عيسى بن مريم يخلق

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r6.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r6.claim: Umar says his suggestion to pray behind the Station of Abraham preceded the revelation permitting it.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r6.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال عمر: وافقت ربي في أربع قلت: يا رسول الله لو صليت خلف المقام

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r7.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r7.claim: Umar suggested a veil for the Prophet's wives because visitors included both righteous and wicked people; the veil verse followed.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال عمر: وافقت ربي في أربع قلت: يا رسول الله لو صليت خلف المقام

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r8.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r8.claim: Umar told the Prophet's wives to desist or God would replace them with better wives, followed by the verse about divorce.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r8.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال عمر: وافقت ربي في أربع قلت: يا رسول الله لو صليت خلف المقام

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r9.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r9.claim: As the creation passage was revealed, Umar uttered this closing praise, which then came as the verse's ending.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r9.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال عمر: وافقت ربي في أربع

DURR-FULL:v6p93/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r10.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r10.claim: While Zayd ibn Thabit dictated the creation passage, Muadh said the closing praise; the Prophet laughed and said the passage had ended with it.
DURR-FULL:v6p93/r10.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت قال: أملى على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v6p94/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p94/r1.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p94/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the creation passage was revealed, Umar said this praise and the phrase was then revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p94/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت {ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين} قال عمر: فتبارك الله

IBNHIBBAN:1977/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1977/r1.speaker: علي رضوان الله عليه
IBNHIBBAN:1977/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet recited a supplication while prostrating that praises God as the best of creators, echoing the verse’s closing words.
IBNHIBBAN:1977/r1.anchor: عن علي رضوان الله عليه قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سجد قال: "اللهم لك سجدت وبك آمنت ولك أسلمت سجد وجهي للذي خلقه وصوره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r8.claim: Thumma marks elevated rank because transforming fluid into congealed blood, with its altered density and color, is more astonishing than the initial creation of the drop.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r8.anchor: وحرف ( ثم ) في قوله : { ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة } للترتيب الرتبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r1.claim: The name alaqa is a remarkable scientific description: anatomy shows the embryo absorbs nourishment from maternal blood through its attachment to uterine veins; alaqa means a piece of clotted blood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r1.anchor: ومن إعجاز القرآن العلمي تسمية هذا الكائن باسم العلقة فإنه وضع بديع لهذا الاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r2.claim: A mudgha is a small piece of flesh about the size of a morsel that can be chewed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r2.anchor: والمضغة : القطعة الصغيرة من اللحم مقدار اللقمة التي تمضغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r3.claim: The author refers readers to the beginning of Surat al-Hajj for the stages of embryonic formation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r3.anchor: وقد تقدم في أول سورة الحج كيفية تخلق الجنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r4.claim: The fa marks a near succession because clotted blood and flesh are close in nature, so their transition is proximate even though each stage lasts a long time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r4.anchor: وعطف جعل العلقة مضغة بالفاء لأن الانتقال من العلقة إلى المضغة يشبه تعقيب شيء عن شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r5.claim: Bones form inside the morsel, beginning the human framework of bone and flesh; this is also indicated by the following clothing of bones with flesh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r5.anchor: وخلق المضغة عظاما هو تكوين العظام في داخل تلك المضغة وذلك ابتداء تكوين الهيكل الإنساني من عظم ولحم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r6.claim: The flesh functions like clothing for the bones; the wording does not require a period when the bones remained without flesh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r6.anchor: فمعنى { فكسونا } أن اللحم كان كالكسوة للعظام ولا يقتضي ذلك أن العظام بقيت حينا غير مكسوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r7.claim: A hadith the author grades sound says each person is a drop for forty days, then a clot for the same period, then a morsel for the same period, after which an angel is sent to breathe in the spirit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح : ( إن أحدكم يجمع خلقه في بطن أمه أربعين يوما نطفة ثم يكون علقة مثل ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r8.claim: The seven stages culminate in a living being; once the spirit is breathed in, life and growth begin, a new condition distinct from the prior lifeless formation, with thumma marking rank.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r8.anchor: فإذا نفخ فيه الروح فقد تهيأ للحياة والنماء وذلك هو المشار إليه بقوله تعالى : { ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r9.speaker: علي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r9.claim: In Umar’s council, Ali answers a claim that withdrawal is minor infanticide by saying an embryo is not infanticide until it passes through the seven stages in the verse; Umar affirms him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r9.anchor: فقال علي : لا تكون موءودة حتى تمر عليها التارات السبع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r10.claim: The report adds that Umar was said to be the first to use the blessing may God prolong your life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p23/r10.anchor: فقيل : إن عمر أول من دعا بكلمة ( أطال الله بقاءك )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r1.claim: Most readers have the plural al-ʿiẓām in both clauses; Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read both forms in the singular.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r1.anchor: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم { عظما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r2.claim: Best of creators means best of makers, since God brings into being what no other can create.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r2.anchor: وفرع على حكاية هذا الخلق العجيب إنشاء الثناء على الله تعالى بأنه { أحسن الخالقين } أي أحسن المنشئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r3.claim: Because human creation most immediately displays immense power, the ensuing praise first celebrates the creator’s wondrous power; baraka conveys increase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r3.anchor: ولما كانت دلالة خلق الإنسان على عظم القدرة أسبق إلى اعتبار المعتبر كان الثناء المعقب به ثناء على بديع قدرة الخالق مشتقا من البركة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r4.speaker: الرَّضي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r4.claim: Al-Raḍi explains that tāfaʿala is originally a form of receiving an action’s effect, and when used like faʿala it conveys intensity because the state becomes firmly established.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r4.anchor: كما صرح به الرضي في ( شرح الشافية )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r5.claim: Tabāraka describes God as possessing immense goodness, namely the great good and welfare He decrees for people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r5.anchor: فمعنى { تبارك الله } أنه موصوف بالعظمة في الخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r6.claim: Omitting the complements of tabāraka and khāliqīn makes the conclusion universal: God’s goodness and creation include humanity, other creatures, mountains, and heavens.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p25/r6.anchor: وبهذا الاعتبار تكون الجملة تذييلا لأن { تبارك } لما حذف متعلقه كان عاما فيشمل عظمة الخير

IBNHIBBAN:1978/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1978/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNHIBBAN:1978/r1.claim: Ali reports that during obligatory prostration the Prophet prayed, affirming faith and surrender and praising God as the best creator.
IBNHIBBAN:1978/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سجد في الصلاة المكتوبة قال

IBNMAJAH:1054/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:1054/r1.speaker: علي
IBNMAJAH:1054/r1.claim: Ali reports that during prostration the Prophet said this prayer of belief and surrender, ending with the verse's praise of God as the best of creators.
IBNMAJAH:1054/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ كَانَ إِذَا سَجَدَ قَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ سَجَدْتُ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r11.anchor: الدم الغريض، والمضغة بضعة اللحم قدر ما يمضغ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r12.claim: A muḍgha is a piece of flesh about the size that can be chewed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r12.anchor: والمضغة بضعة اللحم قدر ما يمضغ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r13.speaker: الجمهور وابن عامر وعاصم والسلمي وقتادة والأعرج والأعمش ومجاهد وأبو رجاء وإبراهيم بن أبي بكير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r13.claim: The majority read plural ʿiẓāman twice; Ibn Amir and Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission use the singular twice; two groups alternate singular and plural in opposite orders.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور عظاما في الموضعين، وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر «عظما» بالإفراد في الموضعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r14.claim: Ibn Masud's reading adds sinews to the bones and says He clothed it with flesh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r14.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود، «ثم جعلنا المضغة عظاما وعصبا فكسوناه لحما»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r15.speaker: ابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية والضحاك وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r15.claim: These authorities identify the new creation as the breathing of the spirit into the embryo.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r15.anchor: فقال ابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية والضحاك وابن زيد: هو نفخ الروح فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the new creation as emergence into the world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: خروجه إلى الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r17.speaker: قتادة عن فرقة
